Surah 11, verses 1–4. It is a Meccan surah.

{1} God Most High says: This is {a Book} that is great and noble in origin. {Its verses have been perfected}, meaning they have been made firm and excellent. Its reports are true, its commands and prohibitions are just, its words are eloquent, and its meanings are radiant. {Then they were made detailed}, meaning they were distinguished and explained with the clearest kind of explanation. It comes {from One who is All-Wise}, who places things in their proper places and assigns them to their proper stations, and who commands and forbids only as His wisdom requires. {All-Aware}, He has knowledge of the outward and the inward. Since its perfection and its detailed explanation come from God, the All-Wise, the All-Aware, do not ask after this about its greatness, its majesty, and its inclusion of perfect wisdom and vast mercy.

{2} God sent down His Book {so that you worship none but God}, meaning for the sake of making the whole religion sincerely devoted to God, and so that none of His creatures associates anything with Him. {Indeed I am} to you, O people, {from Him}, that is from God your Lord, {a warner} to whoever dares to commit sins, with the punishment of this world and the Hereafter, {and a bringer of good news} to those who obey God, with the reward of this world and the Hereafter.

{3} {And seek forgiveness from your Lord} for the sins you have committed, {then turn to Him in repentance} regarding the remaining span of your lives, by returning to Him in devotion and turning away from what God dislikes toward what He loves and approves. Then He mentions what follows from seeking forgiveness and repentance, saying: {He will grant you a good enjoyment} of provision from Him, that you may enjoy and benefit from, {until an appointed term}, that is, until the time of your death. {And He will give} from His bounty {to everyone of bounty his bounty}, meaning He gives those who do good and righteousness from His grace and goodness what is a recompense for their good deeds: the attainment of what they love and the averting of what they dislike. {But if you turn away} from what I have called you to, and indeed turn your backs on it, perhaps even denying it, {then I fear for you the punishment of a great Day}, which is the Day of Resurrection, in which God gathers the earliest and the latest generations.

{4} {To Him is your return}, and He will recompense them for their deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. In His saying {He is Able over all things}, there is something like a proof of God's giving life to the dead. For He is Able over all things, and among all things is the giving of life to the dead, and He has informed us of this, and He is the most truthful of speakers. Therefore the occurrence of this is required both by reason and by transmission.

{5} Almighty God informs us of the ignorance of the polytheists and the intensity of their misguidance: they "fold their breasts" (yathnuna sudurahum), meaning they bend them in order to hide from God. Thus their breasts become a barrier between them and God's knowledge of their conditions, and His sight of their forms. God says, clarifying their error in this assumption: "Ah! When they cover themselves with their garments" (ala hina yastaghshuna thiyabahum), meaning they wrap themselves in them, He knows them in that state, which is among the most concealed of things. Rather, "He knows what they conceal" (ya'lamu ma yusirruna) of sayings and deeds, "and what they reveal" (wa ma yu'linun) of them. Rather, [He knows] what is even more far-reaching than that, which is: "Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts" (innahu 'alimun bidhat al-sudur), meaning of the wills, whisperings and thoughts within them that they have uttered neither secretly nor openly. How, then, could your condition be hidden from Him when you fold your breasts so as to hide from Him?

It is also possible that the meaning here is this: God mentions the aversion of those who deny the Messenger and are heedless of his call, that from the intensity of their aversion they fold their breasts, meaning they hunch over when they see the Messenger, so that he will not see them, make them hear his call, and admonish them with what benefits them. Is there anything beyond this aversion? Then He threatened them with His knowledge of all their conditions, and that they are not hidden from Him, and that He will requite them for their deeds.

{6} That is: every creature that crawls upon the face of the earth, whether human or animal, land-dwelling or sea-dwelling. Allah, exalted is He, has undertaken their provision and sustenance, so their provision is upon Allah. {And He knows their resting-place and their place of storage}; that is, He knows the resting-place of these creatures, which is the place where they remain, settle and take shelter, and their place of storage is the place to which they move in their going and coming and the changing circumstances of their conditions. {All of it} of the details of their circumstances {is in a clear Book}; that is, in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), which contains all the events that have occurred and that will occur in the heavens and the earth. All of them are encompassed by the knowledge of Allah, His pen has run over them, His will has taken effect in them, and His provision has embraced them. So let hearts be at rest in the sufficiency of the One who has undertaken their provision and who encompasses in knowledge their essences and attributes.

{7} He, exalted is He, informs that He {created the heavens and the earth in six days}: the first of them was Sunday, and the last was Friday. {And} when He created the heavens and the earth, {His Throne was upon the water}: above the seventh heaven. Then, after creating the heavens and the earth, He {settled upon His Throne}, governing and directing affairs as He wills, through the decreed commands (al-ahkam al-qadariyyah) and the legislated commands (al-ahkam al-shar'iyyah). Hence He said: {that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed}; that is, that He may try you, since He created for you what is in the heavens and the earth through His command and prohibition, so that He may see which of you is best in deed. Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Its sincerity (ikhlas) and its correctness (sawab)." It was said to him: "O Abu 'Ali! What is its sincerity and its correctness?" He said: "Indeed, if a deed is sincere but not correct, it is not accepted; and if it is correct but not sincere, it is not accepted; until it is both sincere and correct." Sincerity (al-khalis) means that it is for the sake of Allah's face, and correctness (al-sawab) means that it follows the Shari'ah and the Sunnah. This is as Allah, the Exalted, said: {And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me}, and He, the Exalted, said: {Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof. The command descends among them that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge}. So Allah, the Exalted, created the creation to worship Him and to know Him through His names and attributes, and commanded them to do so. Whoever submits and fulfills what he was commanded is among the successful, and whoever turns away from that is among the losers. He will certainly gather them in an abode where He will recompense them for what He commanded them and forbade them. Hence Allah mentioned the disbelief of the polytheists in the recompense, saying: {And if you, [O Muhammad], say, "Indeed, you will be resurrected after death," those who disbelieved will surely say, "This is nothing but obvious magic."}; that is, if you say to these people and inform them of resurrection after death, they will not believe you; rather they will deny you with the utmost denial, disparage what you brought, and say: {This is nothing but obvious magic}; indeed, it is the clear truth.

{8} {And if We delay the punishment for them until a limited nation}; that is, until a determined time, and they consider it slow, they would say, out of their ignorance and wrongdoing: {What holds it back?!} The implication of this is their denial of it; for they infer from its not befalling them promptly that the Messenger who reports the coming of punishment is a liar; how far off is this inference. {Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them}, the punishment, {it will not be averted from them}, so that they may have the opportunity to reflect on their affair, {and there will befall them}; that is, there will descend {what they used to mock}: the punishment, in that they were negligent of it, until they became certain of the lie of the one who brought it.

{9–10} He, exalted is He, informs us about the nature of man: that he is ignorant and wrongdoing. When God lets him taste mercy from Himself, such as health, provision, children and the like, and then takes it away from him, he surrenders to despair and submits to hopelessness. He does not hope for God's reward, nor does it occur to his mind that God will return it to him, or something like it, or something better than it. And when He lets him taste mercy after a hardship that has touched him, he rejoices and becomes exultant, thinking that this good will last for him forever, and says: ﴿Evils have gone away from me; indeed, he is exultant and boastful.﴾ That is, he rejoices in what he has been given that accords with his desires, and he boasts of God's blessings upon His servants. This leads him to insolence, exultation, self-admiration, arrogance toward creation, and contempt and disdain for them. And what fault is worse than this?

{11} This is the nature of man as such, except for those whom God grants success and brings out of this blameworthy disposition to its opposite. They are the ones who restrain themselves in hardship so that they do not despair, and in ease so that they do not exult, and who perform righteous deeds, both obligatory and recommended. ﴿Those will have forgiveness﴾, for their sins, by which every feared harm is removed from them, ﴿and a great reward﴾, which is the success of attaining the Gardens of Bliss, in which is what the souls desire and the eyes delight in.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 11, verses 12–14:

{12} Allah, the Exalted, says, consoling His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) regarding the denial of the deniers: ﴿Perhaps you will leave out some of what is revealed to you, and your breast will be constricted by it, because they say, "Why has a treasure not been sent down to him?"﴾ That is: this is not fitting for one like you; their statement should not affect you or divert you from what you are upon, so that you would leave out some of what is revealed to you and your breast would be constricted by their obstinacy in saying, ﴿"Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or why has an angel not come with him?"﴾ For this statement arises from obstinacy, injustice, stubbornness, error, and ignorance of the places of proofs and evidences. So proceed with your affair, and let not these feeble statements, which proceed only from a fool, turn you back, nor let your breast be constricted on account of them. Have they presented you with an argument you cannot resolve? Or have they disparaged some of what you have brought with a disparagement that affects it and diminishes its worth, so that your breast is constricted on that account? Or is their reckoning upon you, and are you required to guide them by compulsion? ﴿You are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer of all things.﴾ That is: He is the Disposer over them, preserving their deeds and recompensing them for them in the fullest recompense.

{13} ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ That is: Muhammad has invented this Qur'an. So He answered them with His saying: ﴿Say,﴾ to them: ﴿"Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."﴾ That is: indeed, he has invented it; for there is no difference between you and him in eloquence and rhetoric, and you are truly enemies, eager with the utmost of your ability to nullify his call. So if you are truthful, then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated!

{14} ﴿And if they do not respond to you﴾ regarding any of that, ﴿then know that it has been sent down with the knowledge of Allah﴾: from Allah; due to the existence of the evidence and the requirement, and the absence of an opposing factor. ﴿And that there is no deity except Him﴾; that is: and know that there is no deity except Him; that is, He [alone] is deserving of divinity and worship. ﴿Then will you be Muslims?﴾ That is: submitting to His divinity, surrendering to His servitude.

In these verses is guidance that the one calling to Allah should not be deterred by the objections of objectors or the disparagement of detractors, especially when the disparagement has no basis and does not impair what he calls to; and that his breast should not be constricted, but rather he should be reassured by that, proceeding with his affair and attending to his matter. And that it is not obligatory to answer the proposals of those who propose the proofs they choose; rather, it suffices to establish a proof free of opposition on all issues and demands.

And in them: that this Qur'an is inimitable in itself; no one among mankind can bring its like, nor ten surahs like it, nor even a surah like it. For the eloquent and articulate enemies were challenged by Allah with that, yet they did not oppose it, knowing that they had no capacity for it.

And in them: that what is required in it is knowledge and not mere predominance of opinion (ghalabat al-zann): the knowledge of the Qur'an and the knowledge of Tawhid (monotheism); due to His saying: ﴿So know that it has been sent down with the knowledge of Allah, and that there is no deity except Him.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 11, verses 12–14:

{12} Allah, the Exalted, says, consoling His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) regarding the denial of the deniers: ﴿Perhaps you will leave out some of what is revealed to you, and your breast will be constricted by it, because they say, "Why has a treasure not been sent down to him?"﴾ That is: this is not fitting for one like you; their statement should not affect you or divert you from what you are upon, so that you would leave out some of what is revealed to you and your breast would be constricted by their obstinacy in saying, ﴿"Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or why has an angel not come with him?"﴾ For this statement arises from obstinacy, injustice, stubbornness, error, and ignorance of the places of proofs and evidences. So proceed with your affair, and let not these feeble statements, which proceed only from a fool, turn you back, nor let your breast be constricted on account of them. Have they presented you with an argument you cannot resolve? Or have they disparaged some of what you have brought with a disparagement that affects it and diminishes its worth, so that your breast is constricted on that account? Or is their reckoning upon you, and are you required to guide them by compulsion? ﴿You are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer of all things.﴾ That is: He is the Disposer over them, preserving their deeds and recompensing them for them in the fullest recompense.

{13} ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ That is: Muhammad has invented this Qur'an. So He answered them with His saying: ﴿Say,﴾ to them: ﴿"Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."﴾ That is: indeed, he has invented it; for there is no difference between you and him in eloquence and rhetoric, and you are truly enemies, eager with the utmost of your ability to nullify his call. So if you are truthful, then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated!

{14} ﴿And if they do not respond to you﴾ regarding any of that, ﴿then know that it has been sent down with the knowledge of Allah﴾: from Allah; due to the existence of the evidence and the requirement, and the absence of an opposing factor. ﴿And that there is no deity except Him﴾; that is: and know that there is no deity except Him; that is, He [alone] is deserving of divinity and worship. ﴿Then will you be Muslims?﴾ That is: submitting to His divinity, surrendering to His servitude.

In these verses is guidance that the one calling to Allah should not be deterred by the objections of objectors or the disparagement of detractors, especially when the disparagement has no basis and does not impair what he calls to; and that his breast should not be constricted, but rather he should be reassured by that, proceeding with his affair and attending to his matter. And that it is not obligatory to answer the proposals of those who propose the proofs they choose; rather, it suffices to establish a proof free of opposition on all issues and demands.

And in them: that this Qur'an is inimitable in itself; no one among mankind can bring its like, nor ten surahs like it, nor even a surah like it. For the eloquent and articulate enemies were challenged by Allah with that, yet they did not oppose it, knowing that they had no capacity for it.

And in them: that what is required in it is knowledge and not mere predominance of opinion (ghalabat al-zann): the knowledge of the Qur'an and the knowledge of Tawhid (monotheism); due to His saying: ﴿So know that it has been sent down with the knowledge of Allah, and that there is no deity except Him.﴾

{15} He, may He be exalted, says: {Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment}; that is, his entire aspiration is confined to the worldly life and its adornments: women, sons, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle, and tilled land. He has directed his desire, his striving, and his deeds toward these things, and has assigned nothing of his aspiration to the Abode of Permanence. Such a person cannot be anything but a disbeliever, for if he were a believer, the faith he carries would prevent all his aspiration from being directed to the worldly abode. Rather, his very faith and the good deeds that are easy for him are among the effects of his aspiration for the Hereafter. But this wretched person, who seems to have been created for this world alone, {We will pay them in full for their deeds therein}; that is, We will give them what has been apportioned for them in the Mother of the Book of worldly reward. {And in it they will not be deprived}; that is, they will not be shortchanged in anything that has been decreed for them. But this is the limit of their bliss.

{16} {Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire}: abiding therein forever, the punishment never lightened for them, and they are deprived of abundant reward. {And what they did therein has become void}; that is, in the world; meaning it has been nullified and has crumbled away: whatever they did to scheme against the truth and its people, and whatever good deeds they performed that have no foundation and whose necessary condition, which is faith, does not exist.

{17} Almighty God mentions the condition of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and of those who stand in his place among his heirs, who uphold his religion and his proofs, those who are certain of this, and that no one else can be described by their attributes and no one can be like them. He says: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord﴾ — by the revelation in which God sent down the important matters and their clear evidences — so he is certain of that clear proof. ﴿And there follows it﴾; that is, there follows this clear proof and evidence another proof: ﴿a witness from Him﴾ — this is the witness of the upright innate nature (fitrah) and sound reason, which bears witness to the truth of what God revealed and legislated, and by his intellect knows its goodness, so that this increases his faith upon his faith. ﴿And﴾ there is a third witness: ﴿the Book of Moses﴾ — the Torah, which God made ﴿a guide﴾ for people and ﴿a mercy﴾ to them, bearing witness to the truth of this Qur'an and agreeing with it in what it brought of the truth. That is: is one who has this description, upon whom the witnesses of faith have successively come and with whom the evidences of certainty have stood, like one who is in darkness and ignorance and is not coming out of it? They are not equal in the sight of God nor in the sight of the servants of God. ﴿Those﴾; that is, those who were granted success in having the proofs established for them, they believe in the Qur'an in truth, and their faith yields for them every good in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it﴾; that is, in the Qur'an, ﴿of the factions﴾; that is, all the groups of the people of the earth who band together to reject the truth, ﴿then the Fire is his appointed place﴾: he must surely arrive at it. ﴿So be not in doubt about it [i.e., it]﴾; that is, not in the least doubt. ﴿Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe﴾: either out of ignorance and misguidance, or out of injustice, obstinacy and rebellion. Otherwise, whoever has a good intention and a upright understanding will certainly believe in it, because he sees what calls him to faith from every angle.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 11, verses 18–22:

{18} He, the Exalted, informs that there is no one more unjust than ﴿those who invent a lie against Allah﴾. This includes everyone who lies against Allah by ascribing a partner to Him, or describes Him with what does not befit His majesty, or reports about Him what He did not say, or claims prophethood, or any other lie against Allah. These are the greatest of people in injustice. ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord﴾, that He may requite them for their wrongdoing. When He judges them to severe punishment, ﴿the witnesses will say﴾, that is, those who bore witness against them for their fabrication and lying: ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾; that is, a curse that does not end, because their injustice has become a constant attribute of theirs that does not accept lightening.

{19} Then He described their injustice, saying: ﴿who avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾. They averted themselves from the way of Allah, which is the way of the messengers to which they called people, and they averted others from it, so they became leaders calling to the Fire. ﴿And they seek to make it crooked﴾, that is, the way of Allah; they strive to make it deviate, to distort it and to make it appear ugly, so that it becomes crooked in the eyes of people. Thus they make falsehood appear good and make truth appear ugly; may Allah disfigure them. ﴿And they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.﴾

{20} ﴿Those were not to escape [Allah] in the earth﴾; that is, they are not able to outrun Allah, because they are under His power and authority. ﴿And they had no protectors other than Allah﴾, who might ward off harm from them or bring them what benefits them. Rather, their means were severed from them. ﴿The punishment will be doubled for them﴾; that is, it will be intensified and increased, because they went astray themselves and led others astray. ﴿They could not hear﴾; that is, because of their hatred of the truth and their aversion to it, they were unable to hear the signs of Allah in a way that would benefit them. ﴿And why would they be heedless of the reminder? As if they were frightened donkeys fleeing from a lion﴾, ﴿and they could not see﴾; that is, they did not look with the gaze of reflection and contemplation on what would benefit them. They are rather like the deaf and the dumb who do not reason.

{21} ﴿Those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾, for they forfeited the greatest reward and deserved the most severe punishment. ﴿And lost from them is what they used to invent﴾; that is, their religion, which they called to and embellished, has perished, and their deities that they worshipped besides Allah did not avail them when the command of your Lord came.

{22} ﴿Without doubt﴾; that is, truly and certainly, ﴿they will be in the Hereafter the greatest losers﴾. Loss is restricted to them, and indeed they are given its utmost degree, because of the intensity of their regret, their deprivation, and the hardship they suffer from the punishment. So we seek refuge in Allah from their condition.

{23} God, exalted is He, says: {Indeed, those who believe}: with their hearts; that is, they affirmed and acknowledged what God commanded them to believe in of the foundations and principles of the religion. {And do righteous deeds}: which include deeds of the heart and of the limbs, and utterances of the tongue. {And humble themselves before their Lord}: that is, they submitted to Him, were meek before His greatness, and humbled themselves before His authority, and turned to Him in love, fear, hope, and supplication to Him. {Those}: who combined these attributes, {are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever}: because they left no good aim unpursued without attaining it, and no good deed without being foremost to it.

{24} {The likeness of the two parties}; that is, the party of the wretched and the party of the happy, {is like the blind and the deaf}: these are the wretched. {And the seeing and the hearing}: the likeness of the happy. {Are they equal in likeness?}: They are not equal in likeness; rather, between them is a difference that description cannot encompass. {Will you not then remember?}: the deeds that benefit you so that you do them, and the deeds that harm you so that you abandon them.

{23} God, exalted is He, says: {Indeed, those who believe}: with their hearts; that is, they affirmed and acknowledged what God commanded them to believe in of the foundations and principles of the religion. {And do righteous deeds}: which include deeds of the heart and of the limbs, and utterances of the tongue. {And humble themselves before their Lord}: that is, they submitted to Him, were meek before His greatness, and humbled themselves before His authority, and turned to Him in love, fear, hope, and supplication to Him. {Those}: who combined these attributes, {are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever}: because they left no good aim unpursued without attaining it, and no good deed without being foremost to it.

{24} {The likeness of the two parties}; that is, the party of the wretched and the party of the happy, {is like the blind and the deaf}: these are the wretched. {And the seeing and the hearing}: the likeness of the happy. {Are they equal in likeness?}: They are not equal in likeness; rather, between them is a difference that description cannot encompass. {Will you not then remember?}: the deeds that benefit you so that you do them, and the deeds that harm you so that you abandon them.

{25} That is, ﴿And We certainly sent Noah﴾, the first of the messengers, ﴿to his people﴾, calling them to God and forbidding them from polytheism. He said: ﴿Indeed, I am a clear warner to you﴾; that is, I have made clear to you what I warn you of, with a clarity that removes all confusion.

{26} ﴿That you worship none but God﴾; that is, devote worship sincerely to God alone, and abandon everything that is worshipped besides God. ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day﴾ if you do not affirm the Oneness of God and obey me.

{27} ﴿The eminent ones of his people who disbelieved said﴾; that is, the nobles and leaders, rejecting the call of Noah (peace be upon him), as is the habit of such people, for they were the first to reject the call of the messengers: ﴿We see you only as a human being like ourselves﴾. In their view this was an obstacle to following him, although in reality it is the correct position that should not be otherwise, because a human can receive from another human and consult him on every matter, unlike with angels. ﴿And we see none following you except the lowest of us﴾; that is, we see none of us following you except the base and the lowly, in their opinion. In reality, they were the noble and people of intellect, who submitted to the truth. They were not like the base ones who are called the *mala'* (the chiefs), who followed every rebellious devil and took as gods stones and trees, to which they drew near and before which they prostrated. Is there any baser or more contemptible than these? Their saying ﴿at first sight﴾ means: they followed you without reflection or deliberation, but merely at the first call. By this they meant that they were not upon insight in their affairs, and did not know that the clear truth you call to is recognized by the immediate judgment of sound reason, and as soon as it reaches people of understanding, they recognize and affirm it, unlike hidden matters that require long reflection and thought. ﴿And we see in you no superiority over us﴾; that is, you are not better than us so that we should submit to you. ﴿Rather, we think you are liars.﴾ They lied in this saying, for they had seen the signs that God had made as confirmation for Noah, which should have compelled them to a complete certainty of his truthfulness.

{28} Therefore ﴿he said﴾ to them, answering: ﴿O my people, do you see, if I am upon a clear proof from my Lord﴾; that is, upon certainty and conviction. He means: he is the perfect messenger and exemplar, to whom people of understanding submit, and in whose presence the minds of great men are dwarfed; he is truly truthful. So when he says, "I am upon a clear proof from my Lord," this statement suffices as testimony to him and confirmation. ﴿And He has given me mercy from Himself﴾; that is, He revealed to me, sent me, and favored me with guidance. ﴿But it has been made obscure to you﴾; that is, it has been hidden from you, and because of it you were sluggish. ﴿Shall we compel you to it?﴾; that is, shall we force you to accept what we have verified and you doubt? And you are averse, until you were eager to reject what I have brought. That does not harm us, nor does it detract from our certainty concerning it, nor does your saying and your slander against us turn us away from what we were upon. Its ultimate effect is only that it turns you away and causes you not to submit to the truth that you claim is false. So when matters reach this extreme, we cannot compel you to what God has commanded, nor force upon you what you have shunned. Therefore He said: ﴿Shall we compel you to it while you are averse to it?﴾

{29} ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return﴾ for my call to you, ﴾so that you would find the burden heavy﴾; ﴿my reward is only from God﴾. It seems they asked him to drive away the weak believers, so he said to them: ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed﴾; that is, it is not fitting for me nor proper for me to do so; rather I welcome them with warmth, honor, esteem, and reverence. ﴿Indeed, they will meet their Lord﴾, so He will reward them for their faith and piety with gardens of bliss. ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, in that you command me to drive away the friends of God and push them away from me; and in that you rejected the truth because they are its followers; and in that you argued for the falsehood of the truth by your saying: "I am only a human like you, and we have no superiority over you."

{30} ﴿O my people, who would help me against God if I drove them away?﴾; that is, who would protect me from His punishment? For driving them away necessitates punishment and retribution that none can prevent besides God. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ what is most beneficial and proper for you, and reflect upon matters?

{31} ﴿And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of God, nor that I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel﴾; that is, my role is only that I am the messenger of God to you; I give good news and warn. Beyond that, nothing of the affair is in my hand. The treasures of God are not with me, to manage and give to whom I will and withhold from whom I will. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, so as to inform you of your secrets and inner thoughts. ﴿Nor do I say that I am an angel﴾; meaning: I do not claim a rank above my rank, nor a station other than the one God has placed me in, and I do not judge people by my own opinion. ﴿Nor do I say to those whom your eyes despise﴾; that is, the weak believers whom the chiefs who disbelieve look down upon: ﴿God will not grant them any good.﴾ ﴿God knows best what is in their souls.﴾ If they are truthful in their faith, they have abundant good; and if they are otherwise, their account is with God. ﴿Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers﴾; that is, if I said anything of what has preceded. This is a discouragement from him, peace be upon him, to his people, that he would cast off or despise the poor believers, and a persuasion for his people through means that persuade the fair-minded.

{32} When they saw that he did not desist from what he was doing in calling them, and they did not attain their aim from him, ﴿they said: O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation, so bring us what you promise us [of punishment] ﴿if you are among the truthful﴾.﴾ How ignorant and misguided they were, that they said this to their sincere prophet! Why did they not say, if they were truthful: "O Noah, you have advised us, shown concern for us, and called us to a matter that has not become clear to us; so we ask you to make it clear to us that we may submit to you. Otherwise you are to be thanked for your advice." That would have been the fair answer of one who has been called to a matter that is hidden from him. But in their saying they were liars, audacious against their prophet, and they did not refute what he said with the slightest doubt, let alone with proof. Therefore, out of their ignorance and wrongdoing, they turned to hastening the punishment and challenging God.

{33} For this reason Noah (peace be upon him) answered them with his saying: ﴿Only God will bring it upon you, if He wills﴾; that is, if His will and wisdom require that He send it down upon you, He will do so. ﴿And you cannot escape﴾ God; and I have no power over the matter.

{34} ﴿My advice will not benefit you, even if I wish to advise you, if God wills to lead you astray﴾; that is, God's will prevails. If He wills to lead you astray because you reject the truth, then even if I strive to the utmost of my effort and advise you with the most complete advice (and he, peace be upon him, did so), that will not benefit you at all. ﴿He is your Lord﴾; He does with you what He wills and judges concerning you as He desires. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾; He will then recompense you for your deeds.

{35} ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ This pronoun may refer to Noah, as the context of his story with his people indicates, and the meaning is: his people say, "He has invented a lie against God, and denies the revelation which he claims is from God, and that God commanded him to say:" ﴿Say: If I have invented it, upon me is my sin, and I am innocent of what you commit﴾; that is, each one bears his own burden, ﴿and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾. It may also refer to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and this verse would then be an interjection in the course of the story of Noah and his people, because it is among the matters that only prophets know. When God began relating it to His Messenger, and it was among the signs that indicate his truthfulness and messengership, He mentioned his people's denial of him, despite the clear explanation, and said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾; that is, this Qur'an was fabricated by Muhammad from his own self. This is among the most strange and invalid statements, for they know that he could neither read nor write, nor did he travel away from them to study with the people of the scriptures. Yet he brought this Book, with which he challenged them to bring a chapter like it. If, despite this, they claim he invented it, it is known that they are obstinate, and there is no benefit in arguing with them. Rather, in this situation the proper course is to turn away from them. Therefore He said: ﴿Say: If I have invented it, upon me is my sin﴾; that is, my wrongdoing and my lie. ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit﴾; that is, why do you persist in denying me?

{36} His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾; that is, they have become hardened. ﴿So do not grieve over what they have been doing﴾; that is, do not be sad or concern yourself with them and their deeds, for God has detested them and His punishment, which cannot be averted, has become due upon them.

{37} ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and by Our revelation﴾; that is, under Our protection and in Our sight, and seeking Our pleasure. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾; that is, do not argue with Me about their destruction. ﴿Indeed, they will be drowned﴾; that is, the word has already been fulfilled against them, and the decree has been executed upon them.

{38} So he carried out his Lord's command and began constructing the ship. ﴿And whenever a chief of his people passed by him﴾ and saw what he was making, ﴿they mocked him. He said: If you mock us now, ﴾we will mock you as you mock us.﴿

{39} ﴿So you will soon know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him and upon whom there will descend an enduring punishment﴾: we or you? They came to know this when the punishment befell them.

{40} ﴿Until when Our command came﴾; that is, Our decree regarding the time of the descent of the punishment upon them, ﴿and the oven overflowed﴾; that is, God sent down water from the sky in torrents, and caused the whole earth to gush forth springs, even the ovens, which are normally the place of fire and the furthest thing from water, gushed forth. The waters met in accordance with a decree already ordained. ﴿We said﴾ to Noah: ﴿Carry therein two of each kind﴾; that is, of every kind of created thing, a male and a female, so that the species of all kinds would survive. As for the remaining types beyond the pair, the ship could not bear them. ﴿And your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ among those who were disbelievers, such as his son who drowned. ﴿And those who believed﴾, ﴿while﴾ the situation was that ﴿none believed with him except a few.﴾

{41} ﴿And he said﴾, Noah said to those whom God had commanded him to carry: ﴿Embark therein; in the name of God is its course and its anchorage﴾; that is, it sails in the name of God and anchors [in the name of God and sails] by His subjugation and command. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, for He forgave us, showed us mercy, and saved us from the wrongdoing people.

{42} Then He described its sailing as if we were witnessing it, saying: ﴿And it sailed with them﴾; that is, with Noah and those who boarded with him, ﴿through waves like mountains﴾, while God was its guardian and the guardian of its people. ﴿And Noah called to his son﴾ when he was about to board with them, ﴿and he was﴾ in a ﴿separate place﴾ away from them when they boarded; that is, he was far off, and [Noah] wanted him to come near so he could board. He said to him: ﴿O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers,﴾ lest you be struck by what strikes them.

{43} His son, denying his father, replied that no one would be saved except those who boarded the ship: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾; that is, I will climb a mountain and secure myself from the water. Noah said: ﴿Today there is no protector from the command of God except for him upon whom He has mercy﴾; no mountain or anything else protects anyone, even if one takes every possible means. He would not have been saved unless God saved him. ﴿And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned.﴾

{44} When God had drowned them and saved Noah and those with him, ﴿it was said: O earth, swallow your water﴾, that which emerged from you and that which descended upon you; swallow the water that is on your surface. ﴿And O sky, withhold﴾; they obeyed God's command, the earth swallowed its water, and the sky ceased, and the water receded from the earth. ﴿And the matter was decided﴾ by the destruction of the deniers and the salvation of the believers. ﴿And the ship came to rest on al-Judi﴾; that is, it settled upon that well-known mountain in the land of Mosul. ﴿And it was said: Away with the wrongdoing people﴾; that is, they were followed by a curse, and distance and ruin that will not cease to be with them.

{45} ﴿And Noah called to his Lord and said: My Lord, indeed my son is from my family, and Your promise is true﴾; [that is]: You had said to me, "Carry therein two of each kind, and your family," and You will not break what You have promised me. Perhaps he, peace be upon him, was moved by compassion, and because God had promised him the salvation of his family, he thought the promise applied to all of them, both those who believed and those who did not. Therefore he called upon his Lord with that supplication. Nevertheless, he entrusted the matter to the perfect wisdom of God.

{46} God said to him: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family﴾ whom I promised you would be saved. ﴿Indeed, he is unrighteous conduct﴾; that is, this supplication you made for the salvation of a disbeliever who does not believe in God and His Messenger is improper. ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾; that is, what you do not know the outcome and end of, and whether it will be good or not. ﴿Indeed, I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾; that is, I admonish you with an admonition by which you may become among the perfect, and be saved from the qualities of the ignorant.

{47} Then Noah (peace be upon him) felt intense regret for what had come from him, and ﴿said: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge; and unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers﴾. Through forgiveness and mercy the servant is saved from being among the losers. This shows that Noah (peace be upon him) did not know that asking his Lord for the salvation of his son was forbidden, falling under His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they will be drowned﴾. Rather, in his mind the two matters conflicted, and he thought that his son was included in His saying: ﴿and your family﴾. After this, it became clear to him that his son was included among those he was forbidden to pray for and to argue about.

{48} ﴿It was said: O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you﴾; that is, of human beings and others, from the pairs he carried with him. God blessed all of them, until they filled the regions and corners of the earth. ﴿And there will be nations We will grant enjoyment﴾ in this world, ﴿then a painful punishment will touch them from Us﴾; that is, this salvation is not a barrier to Us from bringing punishment upon whoever disbelieves after that. Even if they enjoy briefly, they will be seized afterward.

{49} God said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), after relating to him this detailed story which none knows except one upon whom He has bestowed His message: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew it before this﴾, lest they say that he already knew it. So praise God, thank Him, and be patient in what you are upon of the upright religion, the straight path, and calling to God. ﴿Indeed, the final outcome is for the righteous﴾, who guard against polytheism and all other sins. You will have the final outcome over your people, just as it was for Noah over his people.

{25} That is, ﴿And We certainly sent Noah﴾, the first of the messengers, ﴿to his people﴾, calling them to God and forbidding them from polytheism. He said: ﴿Indeed, I am a clear warner to you﴾; that is, I have made clear to you what I warn you of, with a clarity that removes all confusion.

{26} ﴿That you worship none but God﴾; that is, devote worship sincerely to God alone, and abandon everything that is worshipped besides God. ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day﴾ if you do not affirm the Oneness of God and obey me.

{27} ﴿The eminent ones of his people who disbelieved said﴾; that is, the nobles and leaders, rejecting the call of Noah (peace be upon him), as is the habit of such people, for they were the first to reject the call of the messengers: ﴿We see you only as a human being like ourselves﴾. In their view this was an obstacle to following him, although in reality it is the correct position that should not be otherwise, because a human can receive from another human and consult him on every matter, unlike with angels. ﴿And we see none following you except the lowest of us﴾; that is, we see none of us following you except the base and the lowly, in their opinion. In reality, they were the noble and people of intellect, who submitted to the truth. They were not like the base ones who are called the *mala'* (the chiefs), who followed every rebellious devil and took as gods stones and trees, to which they drew near and before which they prostrated. Is there any baser or more contemptible than these? Their saying ﴿at first sight﴾ means: they followed you without reflection or deliberation, but merely at the first call. By this they meant that they were not upon insight in their affairs, and did not know that the clear truth you call to is recognized by the immediate judgment of sound reason, and as soon as it reaches people of understanding, they recognize and affirm it, unlike hidden matters that require long reflection and thought. ﴿And we see in you no superiority over us﴾; that is, you are not better than us so that we should submit to you. ﴿Rather, we think you are liars.﴾ They lied in this saying, for they had seen the signs that God had made as confirmation for Noah, which should have compelled them to a complete certainty of his truthfulness.

{28} Therefore ﴿he said﴾ to them, answering: ﴿O my people, do you see, if I am upon a clear proof from my Lord﴾; that is, upon certainty and conviction. He means: he is the perfect messenger and exemplar, to whom people of understanding submit, and in whose presence the minds of great men are dwarfed; he is truly truthful. So when he says, "I am upon a clear proof from my Lord," this statement suffices as testimony to him and confirmation. ﴿And He has given me mercy from Himself﴾; that is, He revealed to me, sent me, and favored me with guidance. ﴿But it has been made obscure to you﴾; that is, it has been hidden from you, and because of it you were sluggish. ﴿Shall we compel you to it?﴾; that is, shall we force you to accept what we have verified and you doubt? And you are averse, until you were eager to reject what I have brought. That does not harm us, nor does it detract from our certainty concerning it, nor does your saying and your slander against us turn us away from what we were upon. Its ultimate effect is only that it turns you away and causes you not to submit to the truth that you claim is false. So when matters reach this extreme, we cannot compel you to what God has commanded, nor force upon you what you have shunned. Therefore He said: ﴿Shall we compel you to it while you are averse to it?﴾

{29} ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return﴾ for my call to you, ﴾so that you would find the burden heavy﴾; ﴿my reward is only from God﴾. It seems they asked him to drive away the weak believers, so he said to them: ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed﴾; that is, it is not fitting for me nor proper for me to do so; rather I welcome them with warmth, honor, esteem, and reverence. ﴿Indeed, they will meet their Lord﴾, so He will reward them for their faith and piety with gardens of bliss. ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, in that you command me to drive away the friends of God and push them away from me; and in that you rejected the truth because they are its followers; and in that you argued for the falsehood of the truth by your saying: "I am only a human like you, and we have no superiority over you."

{30} ﴿O my people, who would help me against God if I drove them away?﴾; that is, who would protect me from His punishment? For driving them away necessitates punishment and retribution that none can prevent besides God. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ what is most beneficial and proper for you, and reflect upon matters?

{31} ﴿And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of God, nor that I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel﴾; that is, my role is only that I am the messenger of God to you; I give good news and warn. Beyond that, nothing of the affair is in my hand. The treasures of God are not with me, to manage and give to whom I will and withhold from whom I will. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, so as to inform you of your secrets and inner thoughts. ﴿Nor do I say that I am an angel﴾; meaning: I do not claim a rank above my rank, nor a station other than the one God has placed me in, and I do not judge people by my own opinion. ﴿Nor do I say to those whom your eyes despise﴾; that is, the weak believers whom the chiefs who disbelieve look down upon: ﴿God will not grant them any good.﴾ ﴿God knows best what is in their souls.﴾ If they are truthful in their faith, they have abundant good; and if they are otherwise, their account is with God. ﴿Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers﴾; that is, if I said anything of what has preceded. This is a discouragement from him, peace be upon him, to his people, that he would cast off or despise the poor believers, and a persuasion for his people through means that persuade the fair-minded.

{32} When they saw that he did not desist from what he was doing in calling them, and they did not attain their aim from him, ﴿they said: O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation, so bring us what you promise us [of punishment] ﴿if you are among the truthful﴾.﴾ How ignorant and misguided they were, that they said this to their sincere prophet! Why did they not say, if they were truthful: "O Noah, you have advised us, shown concern for us, and called us to a matter that has not become clear to us; so we ask you to make it clear to us that we may submit to you. Otherwise you are to be thanked for your advice." That would have been the fair answer of one who has been called to a matter that is hidden from him. But in their saying they were liars, audacious against their prophet, and they did not refute what he said with the slightest doubt, let alone with proof. Therefore, out of their ignorance and wrongdoing, they turned to hastening the punishment and challenging God.

{33} For this reason Noah (peace be upon him) answered them with his saying: ﴿Only God will bring it upon you, if He wills﴾; that is, if His will and wisdom require that He send it down upon you, He will do so. ﴿And you cannot escape﴾ God; and I have no power over the matter.

{34} ﴿My advice will not benefit you, even if I wish to advise you, if God wills to lead you astray﴾; that is, God's will prevails. If He wills to lead you astray because you reject the truth, then even if I strive to the utmost of my effort and advise you with the most complete advice (and he, peace be upon him, did so), that will not benefit you at all. ﴿He is your Lord﴾; He does with you what He wills and judges concerning you as He desires. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾; He will then recompense you for your deeds.

{35} ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ This pronoun may refer to Noah, as the context of his story with his people indicates, and the meaning is: his people say, "He has invented a lie against God, and denies the revelation which he claims is from God, and that God commanded him to say:" ﴿Say: If I have invented it, upon me is my sin, and I am innocent of what you commit﴾; that is, each one bears his own burden, ﴿and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾. Yet he brought this Book, with which he challenged them to bring a chapter like it. If, despite this, they claim he invented it, it is known that they are obstinate, and there is no benefit in arguing with them. Rather, in this situation the proper course is to turn away from them. Therefore He said: ﴿Say: If I have invented it, upon me is my sin﴾; that is, my wrongdoing and my lie. ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit﴾; that is, why do you persist in denying me?

{36} His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾; that is, they have become hardened. ﴿So do not grieve over what they have been doing﴾; that is, do not be sad or concern yourself with them and their deeds, for God has detested them and His punishment, which cannot be averted, has become due upon them.

{37} ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and by Our revelation﴾; that is, under Our protection and in Our sight, and seeking Our pleasure. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾; that is, do not argue with Me about their destruction. ﴿Indeed, they will be drowned﴾; that is, the word has already been fulfilled against them, and the decree has been executed upon them.

{38} So he carried out his Lord's command and began constructing the ship. ﴿And whenever a chief of his people passed by him﴾ and saw what he was making, ﴿they mocked him. He said: If you mock us now, ﴾we will mock you as you mock us.﴿

{39} ﴿So you will soon know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him and upon whom there will descend an enduring punishment﴾: we or you? They came to know this when the punishment befell them.

{40} ﴿Until when Our command came﴾; that is, Our decree regarding the time of the descent of the punishment upon them, ﴿and the oven overflowed﴾; that is, God sent down water from the sky in torrents, and caused the whole earth to gush forth springs, even the ovens, which are normally the place of fire and the furthest thing from water, gushed forth. The waters met in accordance with a decree already ordained. ﴿We said﴾ to Noah: ﴿Carry therein two of each kind﴾; that is, of every kind of created thing, a male and a female, so that the species of all kinds would survive. As for the remaining types beyond the pair, the ship could not bear them. ﴿And your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ among those who were disbelievers, such as his son who drowned. ﴿And those who believed﴾, ﴿while﴾ the situation was that ﴿none believed with him except a few.﴾

{41} ﴿And he said﴾, Noah said to those whom God had commanded him to carry: ﴿Embark therein; in the name of God is its course and its anchorage﴾; that is, it sails in the name of God and anchors [in the name of God and sails] by His subjugation and command. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, for He forgave us, showed us mercy, and saved us from the wrongdoing people.

{43} His son, denying his father, replied that no one would be saved except those who boarded the ship: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾; that is, I will climb a mountain and secure myself from the water. Noah said: ﴿Today there is no protector from the command of God except for him upon whom He has mercy﴾; no mountain or anything else protects anyone, even if one takes every possible means. He would not have been saved unless God saved him. ﴿And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned.﴾

{44} When God had drowned them and saved Noah and those with him, ﴿it was said: O earth, swallow your water﴾, that which emerged from you and that which descended upon you; swallow the water that is on your surface. ﴿And O sky, withhold﴾; they obeyed God's command, the earth swallowed its water, and the sky ceased, and the water receded from the earth. ﴿And the matter was decided﴾ by the destruction of the deniers and the salvation of the believers. ﴿And the ship came to rest on al-Judi﴾; that is, it settled upon that well-known mountain in the land of Mosul. ﴿And it was said: Away with the wrongdoing people﴾; that is, they were followed by a curse, and distance and ruin that will not cease to be with them.

{45} ﴿And Noah called to his Lord and said: My Lord, indeed my son is from my family, and Your promise is true﴾; [that is]: You had said to me, "Carry therein two of each kind, and your family," and You will not break what You have promised me. Perhaps he, peace be upon him, was moved by compassion, and because God had promised him the salvation of his family, he thought the promise applied to all of them, both those who believed and those who did not. Therefore he called upon his Lord with that supplication. Nevertheless, he entrusted the matter to the perfect wisdom of God.

{46} God said to him: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family﴾ whom I promised you would be saved. ﴿Indeed, he is unrighteous conduct﴾; that is, this supplication you made for the salvation of a disbeliever who does not believe in God and His Messenger is improper. ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾; that is, what you do not know the outcome and end of, and whether it will be good or not. ﴿Indeed, I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾; that is, I admonish you with an admonition by which you may become among the perfect, and be saved from the qualities of the ignorant.

{47} Then Noah (peace be upon him) felt intense regret for what had come from him, and ﴿said: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge; and unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers﴾. After this, it became clear to him that his son was included among those he was forbidden to pray for and to argue about.

{48} ﴿It was said: O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you﴾; that is, of human beings and others, from the pairs he carried with him. God blessed all of them, until they filled the regions and corners of the earth. ﴿And there will be nations We will grant enjoyment﴾ in this world, ﴿then a painful punishment will touch them from Us﴾; that is, this salvation is not a barrier to Us from bringing punishment upon whoever disbelieves after that. Even if they enjoy briefly, they will be seized afterward.

{49} God said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), after relating to him this detailed story which none knows except one upon whom He has bestowed His message: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew it before this﴾, lest they say that he already knew it. So praise God, thank Him, and be patient in what you are upon of the upright religion, the straight path, and calling to God. ﴿Indeed, the final outcome is for the righteous﴾, who guard against polytheism and all other sins. You will have the final outcome over your people, just as it was for Noah over his people.

{25} That is, ﴿And We certainly sent Noah﴾, the first of the messengers, ﴿to his people﴾, calling them to God and forbidding them from polytheism. He said: ﴿Indeed, I am a clear warner to you﴾; that is, I have made clear to you what I warn you of, with a clarity that removes all confusion.

{26} ﴿That you worship none but God﴾; that is, devote worship sincerely to God alone, and abandon everything that is worshipped besides God. ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day﴾ if you do not affirm the Oneness of God and obey me.

{27} ﴿The eminent ones of his people who disbelieved said﴾; that is, the nobles and leaders, rejecting the call of Noah (peace be upon him), as is the habit of such people, for they were the first to reject the call of the messengers: ﴿We see you only as a human being like ourselves﴾. In their view this was an obstacle to following him, although in reality it is the correct position that should not be otherwise, because a human can receive from another human and consult him on every matter, unlike with angels. ﴿And we see none following you except the lowest of us﴾; that is, we see none of us following you except the base and the lowly, in their opinion. In reality, they were the noble and people of intellect, who submitted to the truth. They were not like the base ones who are called the *mala'* (the chiefs), who followed every rebellious devil and took as gods stones and trees, to which they drew near and before which they prostrated. Is there any baser or more contemptible than these? Their saying ﴿at first sight﴾ means: they followed you without reflection or deliberation, but merely at the first call. By this they meant that they were not upon insight in their affairs, and did not know that the clear truth you call to is recognized by the immediate judgment of sound reason, and as soon as it reaches people of understanding, they recognize and affirm it, unlike hidden matters that require long reflection and thought. ﴿And we see in you no superiority over us﴾; that is, you are not better than us so that we should submit to you. ﴿Rather, we think you are liars.﴾ They lied in this saying, for they had seen the signs that God had made as confirmation for Noah, which should have compelled them to a complete certainty of his truthfulness.

{28} Therefore ﴿he said﴾ to them, answering: ﴿O my people, do you see, if I am upon a clear proof from my Lord﴾; that is, upon certainty and conviction. He means: he is the perfect messenger and exemplar, to whom people of understanding submit, and in whose presence the minds of great men are dwarfed; he is truly truthful. So when he says, "I am upon a clear proof from my Lord," this statement suffices as testimony to him and confirmation. ﴿And He has given me mercy from Himself﴾; that is, He revealed to me, sent me, and favored me with guidance. ﴿But it has been made obscure to you﴾; that is, it has been hidden from you, and because of it you were sluggish. ﴿Shall we compel you to it?﴾; that is, shall we force you to accept what we have verified and you doubt? And you are averse, until you were eager to reject what I have brought. That does not harm us, nor does it detract from our certainty concerning it, nor does your saying and your slander against us turn us away from what we were upon. Its ultimate effect is only that it turns you away and causes you not to submit to the truth that you claim is false. So when matters reach this extreme, we cannot compel you to what God has commanded, nor force upon you what you have shunned. Therefore He said: ﴿Shall we compel you to it while you are averse to it?﴾

{29} ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return﴾ for my call to you, ﴾so that you would find the burden heavy﴾; ﴿my reward is only from God﴾. It seems they asked him to drive away the weak believers, so he said to them: ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed﴾; that is, it is not fitting for me nor proper for me to do so; rather I welcome them with warmth, honor, esteem, and reverence. ﴿Indeed, they will meet their Lord﴾, so He will reward them for their faith and piety with gardens of bliss. ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, in that you command me to drive away the friends of God and push them away from me; and in that you rejected the truth because they are its followers; and in that you argued for the falsehood of the truth by your saying: "I am only a human like you, and we have no superiority over you."

{30} ﴿O my people, who would help me against God if I drove them away?﴾; that is, who would protect me from His punishment? For driving them away necessitates punishment and retribution that none can prevent besides God. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ what is most beneficial and proper for you, and reflect upon matters?

{31} ﴿And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of God, nor that I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel﴾; that is, my role is only that I am the messenger of God to you; I give good news and warn. Beyond that, nothing of the affair is in my hand. The treasures of God are not with me, to manage and give to whom I will and withhold from whom I will. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, so as to inform you of your secrets and inner thoughts. ﴿Nor do I say that I am an angel﴾; meaning: I do not claim a rank above my rank, nor a station other than the one God has placed me in, and I do not judge people by my own opinion. ﴿Nor do I say to those whom your eyes despise﴾; that is, the weak believers whom the chiefs who disbelieve look down upon: ﴿God will not grant them any good.﴾ ﴿God knows best what is in their souls.﴾ If they are truthful in their faith, they have abundant good; and if they are otherwise, their account is with God. ﴿Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers﴾; that is, if I said anything of what has preceded. This is a discouragement from him, peace be upon him, to his people, that he would cast off or despise the poor believers, and a persuasion for his people through means that persuade the fair-minded.

{32} When they saw that he did not desist from what he was doing in calling them, and they did not attain their aim from him, ﴿they said: O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation, so bring us what you promise us [of punishment] ﴿if you are among the truthful﴾.﴾ How ignorant and misguided they were, that they said this to their sincere prophet! Why did they not say, if they were truthful: "O Noah, you have advised us, shown concern for us, and called us to a matter that has not become clear to us; so we ask you to make it clear to us that we may submit to you. Otherwise you are to be thanked for your advice." That would have been the fair answer of one who has been called to a matter that is hidden from him. But in their saying they were liars, audacious against their prophet, and they did not refute what he said with the slightest doubt, let alone with proof. Therefore, out of their ignorance and wrongdoing, they turned to hastening the punishment and challenging God.

{33} For this reason Noah (peace be upon him) answered them with his saying: ﴿Only God will bring it upon you, if He wills﴾; that is, if His will and wisdom require that He send it down upon you, He will do so. ﴿And you cannot escape﴾ God; and I have no power over the matter.

{34} ﴿My advice will not benefit you, even if I wish to advise you, if God wills to lead you astray﴾; that is, God's will prevails. If He wills to lead you astray because you reject the truth, then even if I strive to the utmost of my effort and advise you with the most complete advice (and he, peace be upon him, did so), that will not benefit you at all. ﴿He is your Lord﴾; He does with you what He wills and judges concerning you as He desires. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾; He will then recompense you for your deeds.

{35} ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ This pronoun may refer to Noah, as the context of his story with his people indicates, and the meaning is: his people say, "He has invented a lie against God, and denies the revelation which he claims is from God, and that God commanded him to say:" ﴿Say: If I have invented it, upon me is my sin, and I am innocent of what you commit﴾; that is, each one bears his own burden, ﴿and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾. It may also refer to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and this verse would then be an interjection in the course of the story of Noah and his people, because it is among the matters that only prophets know. When God began relating it to His Messenger, and it was among the signs that indicate his truthfulness and messengership, He mentioned his people's denial of him, despite the clear explanation, and said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾; that is, this Qur'an was fabricated by Muhammad from his own self. This is among the most strange and invalid statements, for they know that he could neither read nor write, nor did he travel away from them to study with the people of the scriptures. Yet he brought this Book, with which he challenged them to bring a chapter like it. If, despite this, they claim he invented it, it is known that they are obstinate, and there is no benefit in arguing with them. Rather, in this situation the proper course is to turn away from them. Therefore He said: ﴿Say: If I have invented it, upon me is my sin﴾; that is, my wrongdoing and my lie. ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit﴾; that is, why do you persist in denying me?

{36} His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾; that is, they have become hardened. ﴿So do not grieve over what they have been doing﴾; that is, do not be sad or concern yourself with them and their deeds, for God has detested them and His punishment, which cannot be averted, has become due upon them.

{37} ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and by Our revelation﴾; that is, under Our protection and in Our sight, and seeking Our pleasure. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾; that is, do not argue with Me about their destruction. ﴿Indeed, they will be drowned﴾; that is, the word has already been fulfilled against them, and the decree has been executed upon them.

{38} So he carried out his Lord's command and began constructing the ship. ﴿And whenever a chief of his people passed by him﴾ and saw what he was making, ﴿they mocked him. He said: If you mock us now, ﴾we will mock you as you mock us.﴿

{39} ﴿So you will soon know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him and upon whom there will descend an enduring punishment﴾: we or you? They came to know this when the punishment befell them.

{40} ﴿Until when Our command came﴾; that is, Our decree regarding the time of the descent of the punishment upon them, ﴿and the oven overflowed﴾; that is, God sent down water from the sky in torrents, and caused the whole earth to gush forth springs, even the ovens, which are normally the place of fire and the furthest thing from water, gushed forth. The waters met in accordance with a decree already ordained. ﴿We said﴾ to Noah: ﴿Carry therein two of each kind﴾; that is, of every kind of created thing, a male and a female, so that the species of all kinds would survive. As for the remaining types beyond the pair, the ship could not bear them. ﴿And your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ among those who were disbelievers, such as his son who drowned. ﴿And those who believed﴾, ﴿while﴾ the situation was that ﴿none believed with him except a few.﴾

{41} ﴿And he said﴾, Noah said to those whom God had commanded him to carry: ﴿Embark therein; in the name of God is its course and its anchorage﴾; that is, it sails in the name of God and anchors [in the name of God and sails] by His subjugation and command. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, for He forgave us, showed us mercy, and saved us from the wrongdoing people.

{42} Then He described its sailing as if we were witnessing it, saying: ﴿And it sailed with them﴾; that is, with Noah and those who boarded with him, ﴿through waves like mountains﴾, while God was its guardian and the guardian of its people. ﴿And Noah called to his son﴾ when he was about to board with them, ﴿and he was﴾ in a ﴿separate place﴾ away from them when they boarded; that is, he was far off, and [Noah] wanted him to come near so he could board. He said to him: ﴿O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers,﴾ lest you be struck by what strikes them.

{43} His son, denying his father, replied that no one would be saved except those who boarded the ship: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾; that is, I will climb a mountain and secure myself from the water. Noah said: ﴿Today there is no protector from the command of God except for him upon whom He has mercy﴾; no mountain or anything else protects anyone, even if one takes every possible means. He would not have been saved unless God saved him. ﴿And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned.﴾

{44} When God had drowned them and saved Noah and those with him, ﴿it was said: O earth, swallow your water﴾, that which emerged from you and that which descended upon you; swallow the water that is on your surface. ﴿And O sky, withhold﴾; they obeyed God's command, the earth swallowed its water, and the sky ceased, and the water receded from the earth. ﴿And the matter was decided﴾ by the destruction of the deniers and the salvation of the believers. ﴿And the ship came to rest on al-Judi﴾; that is, it settled upon that well-known mountain in the land of Mosul. ﴿And it was said: Away with the wrongdoing people﴾; that is, they were followed by a curse, and distance and ruin that will not cease to be with them.

{45} ﴿And Noah called to his Lord and said: My Lord, indeed my son is from my family, and Your promise is true﴾; [that is]: You had said to me, "Carry therein two of each kind, and your family," and You will not break what You have promised me. Perhaps he, peace be upon him, was moved by compassion, and because God had promised him the salvation of his family, he thought the promise applied to all of them, both those who believed and those who did not. Therefore he called upon his Lord with that supplication. Nevertheless, he entrusted the matter to the perfect wisdom of God.

{46} God said to him: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family﴾ whom I promised you would be saved. ﴿Indeed, he is unrighteous conduct﴾; that is, this supplication you made for the salvation of a disbeliever who does not believe in God and His Messenger is improper. ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾; that is, what you do not know the outcome and end of, and whether it will be good or not. ﴿Indeed, I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾; that is, I admonish you with an admonition by which you may become among the perfect, and be saved from the qualities of the ignorant.

{47} Then Noah (peace be upon him) felt intense regret for what had come from him, and ﴿said: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge; and unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers﴾. Through forgiveness and mercy the servant is saved from being among the losers. This shows that Noah (peace be upon him) did not know that asking his Lord for the salvation of his son was forbidden, falling under His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they will be drowned﴾. Rather, in his mind the two matters conflicted, and he thought that his son was included in His saying: ﴿and your family﴾. After this, it became clear to him that his son was included among those he was forbidden to pray for and to argue about.

{48} ﴿It was said: O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you﴾; that is, of human beings and others, from the pairs he carried with him. God blessed all of them, until they filled the regions and corners of the earth. ﴿And there will be nations We will grant enjoyment﴾ in this world, ﴿then a painful punishment will touch them from Us﴾; that is, this salvation is not a barrier to Us from bringing punishment upon whoever disbelieves after that. Even if they enjoy briefly, they will be seized afterward.

{49} God said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), after relating to him this detailed story which none knows except one upon whom He has bestowed His message: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew it before this﴾, lest they say that he already knew it. So praise God, thank Him, and be patient in what you are upon of the upright religion, the straight path, and calling to God. ﴿Indeed, the final outcome is for the righteous﴾, who guard against polytheism and all other sins. You will have the final outcome over your people, just as it was for Noah over his people.

{25} That is, ﴿And We certainly sent Noah﴾, the first of the messengers, ﴿to his people﴾, calling them to God and forbidding them from polytheism. He said: ﴿Indeed, I am a clear warner to you﴾; that is, I have made clear to you what I warn you of, with a clarity that removes all confusion.

{26} ﴿That you worship none but God﴾; that is, devote worship sincerely to God alone, and abandon everything that is worshipped besides God. ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day﴾ if you do not affirm the Oneness of God and obey me.

He means: he is the perfect messenger and exemplar, to whom people of understanding submit, and in whose presence the minds of great men are dwarfed; he is truly truthful. So when he says, "I am upon a clear proof from my Lord," this statement suffices as testimony to him and confirmation. ﴿And He has given me mercy from Himself﴾; that is, He revealed to me, sent me, and favored me with guidance. ﴿But it has been made obscure to you﴾; that is, it has been hidden from you, and because of it you were sluggish. ﴿Shall we compel you to it?﴾; that is, shall we force you to accept what we have verified and you doubt? {29} ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return﴾ for my call to you, ﴾so that you would find the burden heavy﴾; ﴿my reward is only from God﴾. It seems they asked him to drive away the weak believers, so he said to them: ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed﴾; that is, it is not fitting for me nor proper for me to do so; rather I welcome them with warmth, honor, esteem, and reverence. ﴿Indeed, they will meet their Lord﴾, so He will reward them for their faith and piety with gardens of bliss. ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, in that you command me to drive away the friends of God and push them away from me; and in that you rejected the truth because they are its followers; and in that you argued for the falsehood of the truth by your saying: "I am only a human like you, and we have no superiority over you."

{32} When they saw that he did not desist from what he was doing in calling them, and they did not attain their aim from him, ﴿they said: O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation, so bring us what you promise us [of punishment] ﴿if you are among the truthful﴾.﴾ How ignorant and misguided they were, that they said this to their sincere prophet! {34} ﴿My advice will not benefit you, even if I wish to advise you, if God wills to lead you astray﴾; that is, God's will prevails. If He wills to lead you astray because you reject the truth, then even if I strive to the utmost of my effort and advise you with the most complete advice (and he, peace be upon him, did so), that will not benefit you at all. ﴿He is your Lord﴾; He does with you what He wills and judges concerning you as He desires. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾; He will then recompense you for your deeds.

{35} ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ This pronoun may refer to Noah, as the context of his story with his people indicates, and the meaning is: his people say, "He has invented a lie against God, and denies the revelation which he claims is from God, and that God commanded him to say:" ﴿Say: If I have invented it, upon me is my sin, and I am innocent of what you commit﴾; that is, each one bears his own burden, ﴿and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾.
