When God began relating it to His Messenger, and it was among the signs that indicate his truthfulness and messengership, He mentioned his people's denial of him, despite the clear explanation, and said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾; that is, this Qur'an was fabricated by Muhammad from his own self. This is among the most strange and invalid statements, for they know that he could neither read nor write, nor did he travel away from them to study with the people of the scriptures. Yet he brought this Book, with which he challenged them to bring a chapter like it. If, despite this, they claim he invented it, it is known that they are obstinate, and there is no benefit in arguing with them. Rather, in this situation the proper course is to turn away from them. Therefore He said: ﴿Say: If I have invented it, upon me is my sin﴾; that is, my wrongdoing and my lie. ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit﴾; that is, why do you persist in denying me?

{36} His saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾; that is, they have become hardened. ﴿So do not grieve over what they have been doing﴾; that is, do not be sad or concern yourself with them and their deeds, for God has detested them and His punishment, which cannot be averted, has become due upon them.

{37} ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and by Our revelation﴾; that is, under Our protection and in Our sight, and seeking Our pleasure. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾; that is, do not argue with Me about their destruction. ﴿Indeed, they will be drowned﴾; that is, the word has already been fulfilled against them, and the decree has been executed upon them.

{38} So he carried out his Lord's command and began constructing the ship. ﴿And whenever a chief of his people passed by him﴾ and saw what he was making, ﴿they mocked him. He said: If you mock us now, ﴾we will mock you as you mock us.﴿

{39} ﴿So you will soon know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him and upon whom there will descend an enduring punishment﴾: we or you? They came to know this when the punishment befell them.

{40} ﴿Until when Our command came﴾; that is, Our decree regarding the time of the descent of the punishment upon them, ﴿and the oven overflowed﴾; that is, God sent down water from the sky in torrents, and caused the whole earth to gush forth springs, even the ovens, which are normally the place of fire and the furthest thing from water, gushed forth. The waters met in accordance with a decree already ordained. ﴿We said﴾ to Noah: ﴿Carry therein two of each kind﴾; that is, of every kind of created thing, a male and a female, so that the species of all kinds would survive. As for the remaining types beyond the pair, the ship could not bear them. ﴿And your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ among those who were disbelievers, such as his son who drowned. ﴿And those who believed﴾, ﴿while﴾ the situation was that ﴿none believed with him except a few.﴾

{41} ﴿And he said﴾, Noah said to those whom God had commanded him to carry: ﴿Embark therein; in the name of God is its course and its anchorage﴾; that is, it sails in the name of God and anchors [in the name of God and sails] by His subjugation and command. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, for He forgave us, showed us mercy, and saved us from the wrongdoing people.

{42} Then He described its sailing as if we were witnessing it, saying: ﴿And it sailed with them﴾; that is, with Noah and those who boarded with him, ﴿through waves like mountains﴾, while God was its guardian and the guardian of its people. ﴿And Noah called to his son﴾ when he was about to board with them, ﴿and he was﴾ in a ﴿separate place﴾ away from them when they boarded; that is, he was far off, and [Noah] wanted him to come near so he could board. He said to him: ﴿O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers,﴾ lest you be struck by what strikes them.

{43} His son, denying his father, replied that no one would be saved except those who boarded the ship: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾; that is, I will climb a mountain and secure myself from the water. Noah said: ﴿Today there is no protector from the command of God except for him upon whom He has mercy﴾; no mountain or anything else protects anyone, even if one takes every possible means. He would not have been saved unless God saved him. ﴿And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned.﴾

{44} When God had drowned them and saved Noah and those with him, ﴿it was said: O earth, swallow your water﴾, that which emerged from you and that which descended upon you; swallow the water that is on your surface. ﴿And O sky, withhold﴾; they obeyed God's command, the earth swallowed its water, and the sky ceased, and the water receded from the earth. ﴿And the matter was decided﴾ by the destruction of the deniers and the salvation of the believers. ﴿And the ship came to rest on al-Judi﴾; that is, it settled upon that well-known mountain in the land of Mosul. ﴿And it was said: Away with the wrongdoing people﴾; that is, they were followed by a curse, and distance and ruin that will not cease to be with them.

{45} ﴿And Noah called to his Lord and said: My Lord, indeed my son is from my family, and Your promise is true﴾; [that is]: You had said to me, "Carry therein two of each kind, and your family," and You will not break what You have promised me. Perhaps he, peace be upon him, was moved by compassion, and because God had promised him the salvation of his family, he thought the promise applied to all of them, both those who believed and those who did not. Therefore he called upon his Lord with that supplication. Nevertheless, he entrusted the matter to the perfect wisdom of God.

{46} God said to him: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family﴾ whom I promised you would be saved. ﴿Indeed, he is unrighteous conduct﴾; that is, this supplication you made for the salvation of a disbeliever who does not believe in God and His Messenger is improper. ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾; that is, what you do not know the outcome and end of, and whether it will be good or not. ﴿Indeed, I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾; that is, I admonish you with an admonition by which you may become among the perfect, and be saved from the qualities of the ignorant.

{47} Then Noah (peace be upon him) felt intense regret for what had come from him, and ﴿said: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge; and unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers﴾. Through forgiveness and mercy the servant is saved from being among the losers. This shows that Noah (peace be upon him) did not know that asking his Lord for the salvation of his son was forbidden, falling under His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they will be drowned﴾. Rather, in his mind the two matters conflicted, and he thought that his son was included in His saying: ﴿and your family﴾. After this, it became clear to him that his son was included among those he was forbidden to pray for and to argue about.

{48} ﴿It was said: O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you﴾; that is, of human beings and others, from the pairs he carried with him. God blessed all of them, until they filled the regions and corners of the earth. ﴿And there will be nations We will grant enjoyment﴾ in this world, ﴿then a painful punishment will touch them from Us﴾; that is, this salvation is not a barrier to Us from bringing punishment upon whoever disbelieves after that. Even if they enjoy briefly, they will be seized afterward.

{49} God said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), after relating to him this detailed story which none knows except one upon whom He has bestowed His message: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew it before this﴾, lest they say that he already knew it. So praise God, thank Him, and be patient in what you are upon of the upright religion, the straight path, and calling to God. ﴿Indeed, the final outcome is for the righteous﴾, who guard against polytheism and all other sins. You will have the final outcome over your people, just as it was for Noah over his people.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 11, verse 50–60:

{50} That is: {And} We sent {to 'Ad}: they were the well-known tribe in al-Ahqaf in the land of Yemen. {Their brother}: in lineage, {Hud}: so that they could be in a position to take from him and to know his truthfulness. He said to them: {Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. You are nothing but fabricators}; that is, he commanded them to worship Allah alone, forbade them from what they were upon of worshipping other than Allah, and informed them that they had fabricated lies against Allah in their worship of other than Him and in their permitting that. He made clear to them the obligation of worshipping Allah and the corruption of worshipping anything besides Him.

{51} Then he mentioned that there was no obstacle preventing them from submitting, so he said: {O my people, I do not ask of you any reward for it}; that is, any payment from your wealth for what I have called you to, lest you say: "This man wants to take our wealth." Rather, I call you and teach you free of charge. {My reward is only from the One who originated me. Will you not then reason?}: regarding what I call you to, and that it necessitates its acceptance, with no obstacle preventing its rejection.

{52} {And O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord}: for what has passed from you, {then turn to Him in repentance}: for what you will face, with sincere repentance and turning back to Allah the Exalted. For indeed, if you do that, {He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain}: with abundant rains by which the earth is made fertile and its goodness increases, {and will add strength to your strength}: for they were among the strongest of people, and for this they said: {Who is mightier than us in strength?}. So he promised them that if they believed, He would add strength to their strength. {And do not turn away}: from Him; that is, from your Lord, {as criminals}; that is, as arrogant ones refusing to worship Him, audacious toward His prohibitions.

{53} They said, rejecting his words: {O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof}: if their intention by "clear proof" was the proof they were proposing, then this is not binding upon the truth; rather, what is binding is that the Prophet bring a sign that indicates the soundness of what he brought. And if their intention was that he had not brought them any proof testifying to the truth of what he said, then they lied in that, for no prophet came to his people except that Allah sent with his hands signs such that mankind would believe the like of them. Even if he had no sign except his calling them to sincerity of religion for Allah alone without partner, and the command to every righteous deed and beautiful character, and the prohibition of every blameworthy character, from shirk with Allah, abominations, injustice and all kinds of evil, along with the qualities that Hud, peace be upon him, possessed, which are found only in the best of creation and the most truthful of them, these would have sufficed as signs and proofs of his truthfulness. Indeed, people of intellect and understanding see that this sign is greater than mere extraordinary events which some people consider to be miracles only.
Among his signs and clear proofs indicating his truthfulness is that he was a single person, with no supporters or helpers, and yet he cries out to his people, calls them, challenges them, and says to them: "Indeed I have put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord." {Indeed I call Allah to witness, and bear witness, you, that I am free from what you associate with Him, besides Him. So plot against me all together, then give me no respite}: they being the enemies who have dominion and power, and who wish to extinguish the light he carries by whatever means, while he is unconcerned with them and does not care for them, and they are powerless and cannot harm him with any evil. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason. Their saying: {We will not abandon our gods for your words}; that is, we will not abandon the worship of our gods merely because of your saying, for which you have established no proof, in their claim. {And we are not going to believe you}: this is their despair of their prophet Hud, peace be upon him, regarding their faith, and that they continue in their disbelief, wandering blindly.

{54} {We only say}: about you, {that some of our gods have struck you with evil}; that is, they have afflicted you with madness and insanity, so that you have begun to rave with what is not rational. Glory be to the One who sealed the hearts of the wrongdoers! How did they place the most truthful of creation, who came with the most rightful truth, in this rank which a rational person would be ashamed to relate about them, were it not that Allah related it of them?!

{55} For this reason Hud, peace be upon him, made clear that he was utterly confident that no harm from them or from their gods would reach him, so he said: {Indeed I call Allah to witness, and bear witness, you, that I am free from what you associate with Him. So plot against me all together}; that is, seek harm against me, all of you, by every means by which you are able to reach me, {then give me no respite}; that is, do not delay me.

{56} {Indeed I have put my trust in Allah}; that is, I have relied in all my affairs upon Allah, {my Lord and your Lord}; that is, He is the Creator of all, our Manager and yours, and He is the One who nurtures us. {There is no creature but that He holds its forelock}: so it does not move or rest except by His permission. So if you were all to gather together to bring harm upon me, and Allah had not empowered you over me, you would not be able to do that; and if He does empower you, it is for a wisdom He intends. {Indeed my Lord is on a straight path}; that is, upon justice, equity, wisdom and praiseworthiness in His decree, His destiny, His legislation and His command, and in His recompense, reward and punishment; His actions do not depart from the straight path by which He is praised and commended.

{57} {And if you turn away}: from what I have called you to, {then I have conveyed to you what I was sent with}: so no responsibility regarding you remains upon me, {and my Lord will replace you with another people}: who will worship Him and not associate anything with Him, {and you will not harm Him at all}: for your harm returns only to you; Allah is not harmed by the disobedience of the disobedient, nor is He benefited by the obedience of the obedient. Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self, and whoever does evil, it is upon it. {Indeed my Lord is, over all things, Guardian}.

{58} {And when Our command came}; that is, Our punishment, by sending the barren wind which leaves nothing it passes over but makes it like crumbled dust; {We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and We saved them from a harsh punishment}; that is, a great and severe punishment which Allah brought down upon 'Ad, so that in the morning none was seen except their dwellings.

{59} {And that was 'Ad}: those upon whom Allah brought what He brought, as wrongdoers, because they {denied the signs of their Lord}: for this reason they said to Hud: "You have not brought us any proof!" Thus it is made clear by this that they were certain of his call, but they were obstinate and denied it. {And they disobeyed His messengers}: because whoever disobeys one messenger has disobeyed all the messengers, since their call is one. {And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant}; that is, one who dominates the servants of Allah with tyranny, {stubborn}; that is, opposing the signs of Allah. So they disobeyed every sincere advisor who was compassionate toward them, and followed every deceiver who wished their destruction. Without doubt, Allah destroyed them.

{60} {And they were followed in this world by a curse}: so at every time and in every generation there is a mention of their vile news and their shocking reports, by which they are remembered, and blame that attaches to them. {And on the Day of Resurrection}: for them there is also a curse. {Unquestionably, 'Ad denied their Lord}; that is, they denied the One who created them, provided for them, and nurtured them. {Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud}; that is, Allah distanced them from every good and brought them near to every evil.

{61} That is: {And} We sent {to Thamud} — and they are the second 'Ad, well known, who dwelt in al-Hijr and the Valley of the Villages — {their brother}, in lineage, {Salih}, the servant and messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who called them to worship Allah alone. So {he said: "O my people, worship Allah}"; that is, make Him alone, and devote the religion sincerely to Him. {You have no god other than Him}: neither among the inhabitants of the heavens nor among the inhabitants of the earth. {He brought you into being from the earth}; that is, He created you from it. Then He said: {and made you inhabit it}; that is, He made you successors in it, bestowed upon you blessings both apparent and hidden, and established you in the earth, so that you build, plant, sow and cultivate whatever you wish, benefit from its usefulness and draw profit from its interests. Just as He has no partner in all of that, do not associate anyone with Him in worship. {So seek His forgiveness}, for what has issued from you of disbelief, polytheism and sins, and refrain from them, {then turn to Him in repentance}; that is, return to Him with sincere repentance and turning back. {Indeed, my Lord is Near and Responsive}; that is, He is near to whoever calls upon Him, whether by a request or by an act of worship, and He responds by giving his request, accepting his worship, and rewarding him with the most excellent reward.

Know that the nearness of Allah, exalted is He, is of two kinds: general and specific. The general nearness is His nearness by His knowledge to all creation, which is mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: {And We are nearer to him than the jugular vein}.

The specific nearness is His nearness to those who worship Him, ask of Him and love Him, which is mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: {Prostrate and draw near} (al-'Alaq 96:19), and in this verse, and in His saying: {And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near; I respond to the invocation of the supplicant} (al-Baqarah 2:186). This kind of nearness requires His kindness and His responding to their supplications and fulfilling their desires. For this reason, His name "the Near" is paired with His name "the Responsive."

{62} When their prophet Salih, peace be upon him, commanded them and encouraged them to devote themselves sincerely to Allah alone, they rejected his call and met him with the most vile response. {They said: "O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this"}; that is, we used to hope in you and expect from you intelligence and benefit. This is their testimony for their prophet Salih that he had always been known for noble character and good qualities, and that he was among the best of his people. But when he brought them this matter, which did not agree with their corrupt desires, they uttered this statement, whose meaning is that you were perfect, and now you have disappointed our expectation of you, and you have become in a state from which no good is hoped. His offense was what they said about him, [namely] their saying: {Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped?} In their view, this was among the gravest disparagements of Salih: how could he disparage their intellects and the intellects of their misguided forefathers? **Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 11, verses 69–83:**

{69} That is: ﴿And Our messengers came﴾ from the noble angels, ﴿to Ibrahim (Abraham)﴾, the Friend (al-Khalil), ﴿with the good news﴾; that is, with the glad tidings of a son, when Allah sent them to destroy the people of Lut (Lot), and commanded them to pass by Ibrahim and give him the good news of Ishaq (Isaac). When they entered upon him, ﴿they said, "Peace." He said, "Peace"﴾; that is, they greeted him with peace, and he returned the greeting. In this there is the legislation of greeting (mashru'iyyah al-salam), that it has never ceased to be part of the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, that the greeting comes before speech, and that the reply should be more emphatic than the initiation. Their greeting was in the verbal sentence (al-jumlah al-fi'liyyah), which indicates renewal, while his reply was in the nominal sentence (al-jumlah al-ismiyyah), which indicates permanence and continuity, and there is a great difference between them, as is known in the science of Arabic grammar ('ilm al-'Arabiyyah). ﴿So he did not delay﴾: Ibrahim, when they entered upon him, ﴿in bringing a roasted calf﴾; that is, he hastened to his household and brought out for his guests a fat calf roasted on hot stones, and he brought it near to them and said, "Will you not eat?"

{70} ﴿But when he saw their hands not reaching toward it﴾; that is, toward that hospitality, ﴿he felt uneasy about them and harbored fear of them﴾: he thought they had come to him with evil and something hateful. This was before he knew their matter. ﴿They said, "Fear not, for we have been sent to the people of Lut"﴾; that is, we are messengers of Allah, sent by Allah to destroy the people of Lut.

{71} And the wife of Ibrahim was ﴿standing﴾, serving his guests, ﴿and she laughed﴾ when she heard of their condition and what they had been sent with, out of amazement. ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub (Jacob).﴾

{72} So she marvelled at that and ﴿said, "Woe is me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman, and this, my husband, is an old man?" These are two obstacles to the existence of a child. ﴿Indeed, this is an amazing thing.﴾

{73} ﴿They said, "Do you wonder at the decree of Allah?"﴾ For His command has no cause for wonder, since His perfect will is executed in everything; nothing is strange to His power, especially in what He arranges and carries out for the people of this blessed household. ﴿The mercy of Allah and His blessings﴾ be upon you, people of the household; that is, His mercy, His favour and His blessings will not cease, and these are the increase of His goodness and kindness and the descent of divine good upon the servant. ﴿Upon you, people of the household. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.﴾ That is, Praiseworthy in His attributes, since His attributes are attributes of perfection, and Praiseworthy in His actions, since His actions are kindness, generosity, benevolence, wisdom, justice and equity. "Glorious" (majid): glory is the greatness and breadth of attributes; so He has the attributes of perfection, and from every attribute of perfection He has the most perfect, most complete and most comprehensive.

{74} ﴿So when the fear had left Ibrahim﴾, which had come upon him because of his guests, ﴿and the good news had reached him﴾ of the son, he then turned to disputing with the messengers concerning the destruction of the people of Lut, and said to them: ﴿"Indeed, in it is Lut." They said, "We are most knowing of who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife."﴾

{75} ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was forbearing﴾; that is, of good character [good] and wide breast, and not angered by the ignorance of the ignorant. ﴿Oft-sighing﴾; that is, humbly imploring Allah at all times. ﴿Repentant﴾; that is, returning to Allah with knowledge of Him, love for Him, turning toward Him and turning away from all others besides Him. Therefore he would argue on behalf of those whom Allah had decreed to destroy.

{76} It was said to him: ﴿"O Ibrahim, turn away from this"﴾, the disputing. ﴿Indeed, the command of your Lord has come﴾ concerning their destruction, ﴿and indeed, there will come upon them a punishment that will not be turned back﴾; so there is no benefit in your argument.

{77} ﴿And when Our messengers came﴾; that is, the angels who had departed from Ibrahim, when they came ﴿to Lut, he was distressed by them﴾; that is, their coming was grievous to him, ﴿and he felt constrained for them, and said, "This is a distressing day"﴾; that is, severe and difficult. For he knew that ﴿his people﴾ would not leave them alone, since they appeared in the form of beardless, smooth-faced youths of utmost perfection and beauty.

{78} And for this reason what he had feared came to pass, so ﴿his people came rushing to him﴾; that is, hastening and racing, desiring his guests for the abomination that they used to commit. For this reason it says: ﴿And before this they had been doing evil deeds﴾; that is, the abomination which no one among the worlds had preceded them in. ﴿He said, "O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you"﴾ than my guests. This is like what Sulayman (Solomon), peace and blessings be upon him, proposed to the two women: that the child in dispute be split, in order to extract the truth. And he knew that his daughters were forbidden to them and they had no right to them; the greatest purpose was to repel this great abomination. ﴿So fear Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests﴾; that is, either you observe the fear of Allah, or you observe me concerning my guests and do not shame me before them. ﴿Is there not among you a right-minded man?﴾ who would forbid you and restrain you. This is evidence of their depravity and their departure from goodness and manliness.

{79} ﴿They said﴾ to him: ﴿"You certainly know that we have no right to your daughters, and indeed you know what we want."﴾ That is, we desire only men, and we have no desire for women.

{80} So Lut's anxiety, peace be upon him, intensified, and ﴿he said, "If only I had against you some power or could take refuge in a strong support"﴾, such as a protecting tribe, ﴿I would have prevented you." This is according to the apparent causes; otherwise, he takes refuge in the strongest support, which is Allah, against whose strength no one can stand.

{81} For this reason, when the matter reached its end and the distress grew severe, ﴿they said﴾ to him: ﴿"Indeed, we are the messengers of your Lord"﴾; that is, they informed him of their condition so that his heart would be reassured, ﴿"They will never reach you"﴾ with harm. Then Jibril (Gabriel) struck them with his wing and blinded their eyes, so they departed threatening Lut with the coming of the morning. The angels commanded Lut to travel by night with his family ﴿with a portion of the night﴾; that is, with part of it, well before dawn, so that they could get far from their town. ﴿And let none of you look back﴾; that is, hasten to depart, let your concern be salvation, and do not turn to what is behind you. ﴿Except your wife; indeed, she will suffer what they will suffer﴾ of the punishment, because she shared her people's sin, and would inform them of Lut's guests whenever guests came to him. ﴿Indeed, their appointment is the morning﴾. So it seems Lut hastened that, and it was said to him: ﴿"Is not the morning near?"﴾

{82} ﴿So when Our command came﴾ with the descent and imposition of the punishment upon them, ﴿We made its highest part its lowest﴾; that is, We overturned their dwellings upon them, ﴿and rained upon it stones of sijjil (baked clay)﴾; that is, stones of intensely hot fire, ﴿layered﴾; that is, consecutive, following whoever had strayed from the town.

{83} ﴿Marked from your Lord﴾; that is, bearing a sign of punishment and wrath. ﴿And they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾, those who resemble the deed of the people of Lut. So let the servants beware of doing as they did, lest there befall them what befell them.

{84} That is, {And} We sent {to Madyan} the well-known tribe who dwelt in Madyan, in the far reaches of Palestine, {their brother} by lineage, {Shu'ayb}, because they knew him and were able to take from him. So he said to them: {O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him}; that is, devote worship sincerely to Him, for they used to associate partners with Him. And along with their polytheism, they used to cheat in measure and weight, so he forbade them from that, saying: {And do not diminish the measure and the scale}; rather, give full measure and weight with justice. {Indeed, I see you in prosperity}; that is, in abundant blessings, health, and great wealth and children. So thank Allah for what He has given you, and do not be ungrateful for the blessing of Allah, lest He remove it from you. {And indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing Day}; that is, a punishment that will encompass you and leave none of you remaining.

{85} {And O my people, give full measure and weight with justice}; that is, with the justice that you would be content to receive. {And do not deprive the people of their things}; that is, do not diminish people's goods, by taking them through shortchanging in measure and weight. {And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption}; for persistence in sins corrupts religions, beliefs, and both this world and the next, and destroys the crops and the offspring.

{86} {What remains with Allah is better for you}; that is, what Allah has left for you of good, and what is rightfully yours, suffices you; so do not covet something for which you have no need, and which is greatly harmful to you. {If you are believers}; then act in accordance with the requirements of faith. {And I am not a guardian over you}; that is, I am not a keeper of your deeds or one appointed over them. Rather, it is Allah, the Exalted, who preserves them; as for me, I convey what I was sent with.

{87} {They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped?"}; that is, they said this mockingly toward their prophet and as a way of deeming his call to be unlikely to be answered. The meaning of their words is: there is no reason for your forbidding us except that you pray to Allah and worship Him. So if you are like that, does it necessitate for us that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, on the basis of a statement for which there is no proof other than that it agrees with you?! How then should we follow you and abandon our forefathers, the people of intellect and understanding?! Likewise, your words do not oblige us to do with our wealth what you have told us, such as giving full measure and weight and fulfilling the obligatory rights concerning it; rather, we will continue to do with it what we wish, for it is our wealth, and you have no authority over it. This is why they said in their mockery: {Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided}; that is, is it you who possesses forbearance and dignity as a character trait, and right guidance as a natural disposition, so that nothing but rightguidance issues from you, and you command only what is right and forbid only what is wrong?! That is, the matter is not so; and their intention was that he was described by the opposite of these two qualities: by foolishness and misguidance. The meaning is: how can you be the forbearing, the rightly guided, while our fathers are the foolish, the astray?! This statement, which they expressed in the form of mockery, and that the matter is the opposite of it, is not as they supposed; rather, the matter is as they themselves said: his prayer commands him to forbid them from what their misguided fathers worshipped, and to do with their wealth what he wishes; for prayer forbids indecency and wrongdoing. And what indecency and wrongdoing is greater than worshipping other than Allah, and withholding the rights of the servants of Allah, or stealing them by means of measures and scales? And he, peace be upon him, was the forbearing, the rightly guided!

{88} {He said}, to them, Shu'ayb: {O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord}; that is, certainty and tranquility regarding the soundness of what I have brought, {and He has provided for me from Himself good provision}; that is, Allah has given me of kinds of wealth what He has given me, {and} I {do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you}: I do not intend to forbid you from shortchanging in measure and weight while doing it myself, so that suspicion might fall upon me in that matter; rather, I do not forbid you from any matter except that I am the first to hasten to abandon it. {I intend only reform as much as I am able}; that is, my only aim is that your conditions be set right and your interests be upright, and I have no aim of my own alone, to the extent of my ability. And since this contains a kind of self-praise, he dispelled that by saying: {And my success is not but through Allah}; that is, the success I attain in doing good and in disengaging from evil is only through Allah, the Exalted, not by my own power or strength. {Upon Him I have relied}; that is, I have depended upon Him in my affairs and trusted in His sufficiency. {And to Him I turn back}: in carrying out what He has commanded me of various kinds of worship, and in drawing near to Him through all acts of goodness. By these two matters the condition of the servant is set right: seeking help from his Lord and turning back to Him, as Allah, the Exalted, said: {So worship Him and rely upon Him}. And He said: {You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help}.

{89} {And O my people, let not my opposition bring upon you}; that is, let not my defiance and hostility lead you, {to be struck by} punishments {like what struck the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih; and the people of Lot are not far from you}: neither in place nor in time.

{90} {And seek forgiveness from your Lord}: for what you have committed of sins, {then repent to Him}: for what remains of your lives, with sincere repentance and turning back to Him by obeying Him and abandoning disobedience to Him. {Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving}: toward whoever repents and turns back; He shows mercy to him, forgives him, accepts his repentance, and loves him.
The meaning of Al-Wadud among His names, the Exalted, is that He loves His believing servants and they love Him; so it is fa'ul in the sense of fa'il and in the sense of maf'ul.

{91} {They said, "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say}; that is, they grew bored of his advice and admonitions to them, and said: we do not understand much of what you say, because of their hatred for what he says and their aversion to him. {And indeed, we see you among us as weak}; that is, in yourself: you are not among the great and the leaders, but among the oppressed. {And were it not for your clan}; that is, your group and tribe, {we would have stoned you, and you are not mighty against us}; that is, you have no station in our hearts and no honor in our souls, and we only honored your tribe by leaving you alone.

{92} {He said}, softening toward them: {O my people, is my clan more mighty to you than Allah?}; that is, how do you show regard for me for the sake of my clan, and do not show regard for me for the sake of Allah, so that my clan has become more mighty to you than Allah. {And you have put Him behind your backs}; that is, you cast the command of Allah behind your backs, and paid no heed to it, and did not fear it. {Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do}: nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him, not an atom's weight on the earth or in the heaven, and He will recompense you for what you have done with the most complete recompense.

{93} {And} when they wearied him and he was unable against them, he said: {O my people, act according to your position}; that is, according to your state and your religion. {Indeed, I am acting; you will know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him}: and upon whom a lasting punishment will descend, I or you. They knew this when the punishment befell them. {And wait}: for what will befall me. {Indeed, I am with you, a watcher} over what will befall you.

{94} {And when Our command came}: to destroy the people of Shu'ayb, {We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the cry seized those who did wrong, and they became in their homes fallen prostrate}: not hearing any sound from them, nor seeing any movement from them.

{95} {As if they had never prospered therein}; that is, as if they had never remained in their homes nor enjoyed comfort in them when the punishment came upon them. {Unquestionably, away with Madyan}: since Allah destroyed them and humiliated them, {just as Thamud were removed}; that is, these two tribes shared in being crushed, removed, and destroyed.
Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, was called the orator of the prophets, because of the excellence of his argumentation with his people. There is much benefit and lesson in his story:
Among them: that disbelievers are punished and addressed with the basics of Islam, and likewise with its laws and branches; for Shu'ayb called his people to monotheism and to giving full measure and weight, and made the threat dependent upon the whole of that.
Among them: that diminishing measures and weights is among the major sins, and immediate punishment is feared for whoever engages in it, and that this is theft of people's wealth; and if their theft by measures and weights entails the threat, then their theft by way of coercion and dominance is more fitting and more deserving.
Among them: that recompense is of the same kind as the deed; whoever cheats people's wealth, desiring to increase his own wealth, is punished with the opposite of that, and it becomes a cause for the loss of the good provision he has; as in His saying: {Indeed, I see you in prosperity}; that is, do not cause its loss by your own actions.
Among them: that the servant should be content with what Allah has given him, and be content with the lawful over the unlawful, and with permissible gains over forbidden gains; and that this is better for him, as in His saying: {What remains with Allah is better for you}; for in that there is blessing and increase of provision that is not found in eagerly pursuing forbidden means, which brings erasure and the opposite of blessing.
Among them: that this is among the requirements and fruits of faith; for He tied acting upon it to the existence of faith, which indicates that if the deed is not present, then faith is deficient or nonexistent.
Among them: that prayer has always been prescribed for the earlier prophets, and that it is among the best of deeds, to the extent that its excellence and its precedence over all other deeds are firmly established even among disbelievers; and that it forbids indecency and wrongdoing; and it is a measure of faith and its laws; so by establishing it the servant's condition is perfected, and by not establishing it his religious condition falls into disorder.
Among them: that the wealth which Allah provides for a person, even if Allah has granted it to him, is not for him to do with as he pleases; for it is a trust with him, and he must uphold Allah's right in it by fulfilling the rights that are due in it and refraining from the gains which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, not as the disbelievers and those like them claim, that their wealth is theirs to do with as they wish and choose, whether it agrees with the ruling of Allah or opposes it.
Among them: that it is part of completing and perfecting the call of the caller that he be the first to hasten to what he commands others to do, and the first to refrain from what he forbids others; as Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said: {And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you}, and as Allah, the Exalted, said: {O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? [It is most hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do]}.
Among them: that the duty, custom, and method of the messengers is to intend reform according to ability and capacity, so they bring about the attainment and perfecting of benefits, or the attainment of what is within their power of them, and the averting and reducing of harms; and they give precedence to public benefit over private benefit.
The reality of benefit (maslahah) is that by which the conditions of the servants are set right and their religious and worldly affairs are made upright.
Among them: that whoever undertakes what he is able of reform is not blameworthy or censured for not doing what he is unable to do; so the servant should establish, in himself and in others, the reform that he is able to.
Among them: that the servant should never rely on himself even for the blink of an eye, but should always seek help from his Lord, depending upon Him, asking Him for success; and if he attains any success, he should attribute it to the One who granted and bestowed it, and not be conceited with himself; as in His saying: {And my success is not but through Allah; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back}.
Among them: the warning through the punishments of nations, and what befell them, and that stories in which punishments are inflicted on criminals should be mentioned in the context of admonition and deterrence; just as it is fitting to mention what Allah has honored the people of piety with when encouraging and urging piety.
Among them: that the repentant from sin, just as he is pardoned and forgiven for his sin, Allah, the Exalted, loves him and is fond of him; and there is no weight to the saying of one who says that when the repentant repents, it is enough for him to be forgiven and for pardon to return to him, while the return of affection and love does not occur; for Allah said: {And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him; indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving}.
Among them: that Allah repels from the believers by many means, some of which they know and some of which they do not know at all; and sometimes He repels from them by means of their tribe and the disbelieving people of their homeland; as Allah repelled from Shu'ayb the stoning of his people by means of his clan.
And that these ties through which defense of Islam and Muslims is achieved are not objectionable to strive in; rather, it may even be required, because reform is sought according to ability and capacity. Accordingly, if Muslims living under the rule of disbelievers were to assist and work to make the rule a republic in which individuals and peoples can secure their religious and worldly rights, it would be better than their submission to a state that abolishes their religious and worldly rights, and seeks their annihilation and their reduction to laborers and servants. Yes; if it is possible for the state to belong to Muslims, with them as rulers, that is what is required; but since this rank is not attainable, the rank in which there is defense and protection for religion and worldly life takes precedence. And Allah knows best.

{84} That is, {And} We sent {to Madyan} the well-known tribe who dwelt in Madyan, in the far reaches of Palestine, {their brother} by lineage, {Shu'ayb}, because they knew him and were able to take from him. So he said to them: {O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him}; that is, devote worship sincerely to Him, for they used to associate partners with Him. And along with their polytheism, they used to cheat in measure and weight, so he forbade them from that, saying: {And do not diminish the measure and the scale}; rather, give full measure and weight with justice. {Indeed, I see you in prosperity}; that is, in abundant blessings, health, and great wealth and children. So thank Allah for what He has given you, and do not be ungrateful for the blessing of Allah, lest He remove it from you. {And indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing Day}; that is, a punishment that will encompass you and leave none of you remaining.

{85} {And O my people, give full measure and weight with justice}; that is, with the justice that you would be content to receive. {And do not deprive the people of their things}; that is, do not diminish people's goods, by taking them through shortchanging in measure and weight. {And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption}; for persistence in sins corrupts religions, beliefs, and both this world and the next, and destroys the crops and the offspring.

{86} {What remains with Allah is better for you}; that is, what Allah has left for you of good, and what is rightfully yours, suffices you; so do not covet something for which you have no need, and which is greatly harmful to you. {If you are believers}; then act in accordance with the requirements of faith. {And I am not a guardian over you}; that is, I am not a keeper of your deeds or one appointed over them. Rather, it is Allah, the Exalted, who preserves them; as for me, I convey what I was sent with.

{87} {They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped?"}; that is, they said this mockingly toward their prophet and as a way of deeming his call to be unlikely to be answered. So if you are like that, does it necessitate for us that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, on the basis of a statement for which there is no proof other than that it agrees with you?! How then should we follow you and abandon our forefathers, the people of intellect and understanding?! {92} {He said}, softening toward them: {O my people, is my clan more mighty to you than Allah?}; that is, how do you show regard for me for the sake of my clan, and do not show regard for me for the sake of Allah, so that my clan has become more mighty to you than Allah. {And you have put Him behind your backs}; that is, you cast the command of Allah behind your backs, and paid no heed to it, and did not fear it. {Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do}: nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him, not an atom's weight on the earth or in the heaven, and He will recompense you for what you have done with the most complete recompense.

{93} {And} when they wearied him and he was unable against them, he said: {O my people, act according to your position}; that is, according to your state and your religion. {Indeed, I am acting; you will know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him}: and upon whom a lasting punishment will descend, I or you. {94} {And when Our command came}: to destroy the people of Shu'ayb, {We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the cry seized those who did wrong, and they became in their homes fallen prostrate}: not hearing any sound from them, nor seeing any movement from them.

{95} {As if they had never prospered therein}; that is, as if they had never remained in their homes nor enjoyed comfort in them when the punishment came upon them. {Unquestionably, away with Madyan}: since Allah destroyed them and humiliated them, {just as Thamud were removed}; that is, these two tribes shared in being crushed, removed, and destroyed.
Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, was called the orator of the prophets, because of the excellence of his argumentation with his people. There is much benefit and lesson in his story:
Among them: that disbelievers are punished and addressed with the basics of Islam, and likewise with its laws and branches; for Shu'ayb called his people to monotheism and to giving full measure and weight, and made the threat dependent upon the whole of that.
Among them: that diminishing measures and weights is among the major sins, and immediate punishment is feared for whoever engages in it, and that this is theft of people's wealth; and if their theft by measures and weights entails the threat, then their theft by way of coercion and dominance is more fitting and more deserving.
Among them: that recompense is of the same kind as the deed; whoever cheats people's wealth, desiring to increase his own wealth, is punished with the opposite of that, and it becomes a cause for the loss of the good provision he has; as in His saying: {Indeed, I see you in prosperity}; that is, do not cause its loss by your own actions.
Among them: that the servant should be content with what Allah has given him, and be content with the lawful over the unlawful, and with permissible gains over forbidden gains; and that this is better for him, as in His saying: {What remains with Allah is better for you}; for in that there is blessing and increase of provision that is not found in eagerly pursuing forbidden means, which brings erasure and the opposite of blessing.
Among them: that this is among the requirements and fruits of faith; for He tied acting upon it to the existence of faith, which indicates that if the deed is not present, then faith is deficient or nonexistent.
Among them: that prayer has always been prescribed for the earlier prophets, and that it is among the best of deeds, to the extent that its excellence and its precedence over all other deeds are firmly established even among disbelievers; and that it forbids indecency and wrongdoing; and it is a measure of faith and its laws; so by establishing it the servant's condition is perfected, and by not establishing it his religious condition falls into disorder.
Among them: that the wealth which Allah provides for a person, even if Allah has granted it to him, is not for him to do with as he pleases; for it is a trust with him, and he must uphold Allah's right in it by fulfilling the rights that are due in it and refraining from the gains which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, not as the disbelievers and those like them claim, that their wealth is theirs to do with as they wish and choose, whether it agrees with the ruling of Allah or opposes it.
Among them: that it is part of completing and perfecting the call of the caller that he be the first to hasten to what he commands others to do, and the first to refrain from what he forbids others; as Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said: {And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you}, and as Allah, the Exalted, said: {O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? [It is most hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do]}.
Among them: that the duty, custom, and method of the messengers is to intend reform according to ability and capacity, so they bring about the attainment and perfecting of benefits, or the attainment of what is within their power of them, and the averting and reducing of harms; and they give precedence to public benefit over private benefit.
The reality of benefit (maslahah) is that by which the conditions of the servants are set right and their religious and worldly affairs are made upright.
Among them: that whoever undertakes what he is able of reform is not blameworthy or censured for not doing what he is unable to do; so the servant should establish, in himself and in others, the reform that he is able to.
Among them: that the servant should never rely on himself even for the blink of an eye, but should always seek help from his Lord, depending upon Him, asking Him for success; and if he attains any success, he should attribute it to the One who granted and bestowed it, and not be conceited with himself; as in His saying: {And my success is not but through Allah; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back}.
Among them: the warning through the punishments of nations, and what befell them, and that stories in which punishments are inflicted on criminals should be mentioned in the context of admonition and deterrence; just as it is fitting to mention what Allah has honored the people of piety with when encouraging and urging piety.
Among them: that the repentant from sin, just as he is pardoned and forgiven for his sin, Allah, the Exalted, loves him and is fond of him; and there is no weight to the saying of one who says that when the repentant repents, it is enough for him to be forgiven and for pardon to return to him, while the return of affection and love does not occur; for Allah said: {And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him; indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving}.
Among them: that Allah repels from the believers by many means, some of which they know and some of which they do not know at all; and sometimes He repels from them by means of their tribe and the disbelieving people of their homeland; as Allah repelled from Shu'ayb the stoning of his people by means of his clan.
And that these ties through which defense of Islam and Muslims is achieved are not objectionable to strive in; rather, it may even be required, because reform is sought according to ability and capacity. Accordingly, if Muslims living under the rule of disbelievers were to assist and work to make the rule a republic in which individuals and peoples can secure their religious and worldly rights, it would be better than their submission to a state that abolishes their religious and worldly rights, and seeks their annihilation and their reduction to laborers and servants. Yes; if it is possible for the state to belong to Muslims, with them as rulers, that is what is required; but since this rank is not attainable, the rank in which there is defense and protection for religion and worldly life takes precedence. And Allah knows best.

{95} {As if they had never prospered therein}; that is, as if they had never remained in their homes nor enjoyed comfort in them when the punishment came upon them. {Unquestionably, away with Madyan}: since Allah destroyed them and humiliated them, {just as Thamud were removed}; that is, these two tribes shared in being crushed, removed, and destroyed.
Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, was called the orator of the prophets, because of the excellence of his argumentation with his people. There is much benefit and lesson in his story:
Among them: that disbelievers are punished and addressed with the basics of Islam, and likewise with its laws and branches; for Shu'ayb called his people to monotheism and to giving full measure and weight, and made the threat dependent upon the whole of that.
Among them: that diminishing measures and weights is among the major sins, and immediate punishment is feared for whoever engages in it, and that this is theft of people's wealth; and if their theft by measures and weights entails the threat, then their theft by way of coercion and dominance is more fitting and more deserving.
Among them: that recompense is of the same kind as the deed; whoever cheats people's wealth, desiring to increase his own wealth, is punished with the opposite of that, and it becomes a cause for the loss of the good provision he has; as in His saying: {Indeed, I see you in prosperity}; that is, do not cause its loss by your own actions.
Among them: that the servant should be content with what Allah has given him, and be content with the lawful over the unlawful, and with permissible gains over forbidden gains; and that this is better for him, as in His saying: {What remains with Allah is better for you}; for in that there is blessing and increase of provision that is not found in eagerly pursuing forbidden means, which brings erasure and the opposite of blessing.
Among them: that this is among the requirements and fruits of faith; for He tied acting upon it to the existence of faith, which indicates that if the deed is not present, then faith is deficient or nonexistent.
Among them: that prayer has always been prescribed for the earlier prophets, and that it is among the best of deeds, to the extent that its excellence and its precedence over all other deeds are firmly established even among disbelievers; and that it forbids indecency and wrongdoing; and it is a measure of faith and its laws; so by establishing it the servant's condition is perfected, and by not establishing it his religious condition falls into disorder.
Among them: that the wealth which Allah provides for a person, even if Allah has granted it to him, is not for him to do with as he pleases; for it is a trust with him, and he must uphold Allah's right in it by fulfilling the rights that are due in it and refraining from the gains which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, not as the disbelievers and those like them claim, that their wealth is theirs to do with as they wish and choose, whether it agrees with the ruling of Allah or opposes it.
Among them: that it is part of completing and perfecting the call of the caller that he be the first to hasten to what he commands others to do, and the first to refrain from what he forbids others; as Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said: {And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you}, and as Allah, the Exalted, said: {O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? [It is most hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do]}.
Among them: that the duty, custom, and method of the messengers is to intend reform according to ability and capacity, so they bring about the attainment and perfecting of benefits, or the attainment of what is within their power of them, and the averting and reducing of harms; and they give precedence to public benefit over private benefit.
The reality of benefit (maslahah) is that by which the conditions of the servants are set right and their religious and worldly affairs are made upright.
Among them: that whoever undertakes what he is able of reform is not blameworthy or censured for not doing what he is unable to do; so the servant should establish, in himself and in others, the reform that he is able to.
Among them: that the servant should never rely on himself even for the blink of an eye, but should always seek help from his Lord, depending upon Him, asking Him for success; and if he attains any success, he should attribute it to the One who granted and bestowed it, and not be conceited with himself; as in His saying: {And my success is not but through Allah; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back}.
Among them: the warning through the punishments of nations, and what befell them, and that stories in which punishments are inflicted on criminals should be mentioned in the context of admonition and deterrence; just as it is fitting to mention what Allah has honored the people of piety with when encouraging and urging piety.
Among them: that the repentant from sin, just as he is pardoned and forgiven for his sin, Allah, the Exalted, loves him and is fond of him; and there is no weight to the saying of one who says that when the repentant repents, it is enough for him to be forgiven and for pardon to return to him, while the return of affection and love does not occur; for Allah said: {And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him; indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving}.
Among them: that Allah repels from the believers by many means, some of which they know and some of which they do not know at all; and sometimes He repels from them by means of their tribe and the disbelieving people of their homeland; as Allah repelled from Shu'ayb the stoning of his people by means of his clan.
And that these ties through which defense of Islam and Muslims is achieved are not objectionable to strive in; rather, it may even be required, because reform is sought according to ability and capacity. Accordingly, if Muslims living under the rule of disbelievers were to assist and work to make the rule a republic in which individuals and peoples can secure their religious and worldly rights, it would be better than their submission to a state that abolishes their religious and worldly rights, and seeks their annihilation and their reduction to laborers and servants. Yes; if it is possible for the state to belong to Muslims, with them as rulers, that is what is required; but since this rank is not attainable, the rank in which there is defense and protection for religion and worldly life takes precedence. And Allah knows best.

Among them: that recompense is of the same kind as the deed; whoever cheats people's wealth, desiring to increase his own wealth, is punished with the opposite of that, and it becomes a cause for the loss of the good provision he has; as in His saying: {Indeed, I see you in prosperity}; that is, do not cause its loss by your own actions.
Among them: that the servant should be content with what Allah has given him, and be content with the lawful over the unlawful, and with permissible gains over forbidden gains; and that this is better for him, as in His saying: {What remains with Allah is better for you}; for in that there is blessing and increase of provision that is not found in eagerly pursuing forbidden means, which brings erasure and the opposite of blessing.

Among them: that prayer has always been prescribed for the earlier prophets, and that it is among the best of deeds, to the extent that its excellence and its precedence over all other deeds are firmly established even among disbelievers; and that it forbids indecency and wrongdoing; and it is a measure of faith and its laws; so by establishing it the servant's condition is perfected, and by not establishing it his religious condition falls into disorder.
Among them: that the wealth which Allah provides for a person, even if Allah has granted it to him, is not for him to do with as he pleases; for it is a trust with him, and he must uphold Allah's right in it by fulfilling the rights that are due in it and refraining from the gains which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, not as the disbelievers and those like them claim, that their wealth is theirs to do with as they wish and choose, whether it agrees with the ruling of Allah or opposes it.
Among them: that it is part of completing and perfecting the call of the caller that he be the first to hasten to what he commands others to do, and the first to refrain from what he forbids others; as Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said: {And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you}, and as Allah, the Exalted, said: {O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? [It is most hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do]}.
Among them: that the duty, custom, and method of the messengers is to intend reform according to ability and capacity, so they bring about the attainment and perfecting of benefits, or the attainment of what is within their power of them, and the averting and reducing of harms; and they give precedence to public benefit over private benefit.
The reality of benefit (maslahah) is that by which the conditions of the servants are set right and their religious and worldly affairs are made upright.
Among them: that whoever undertakes what he is able of reform is not blameworthy or censured for not doing what he is unable to do; so the servant should establish, in himself and in others, the reform that he is able to.
Among them: that the servant should never rely on himself even for the blink of an eye, but should always seek help from his Lord, depending upon Him, asking Him for success; and if he attains any success, he should attribute it to the One who granted and bestowed it, and not be conceited with himself; as in His saying: {And my success is not but through Allah; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back}.
Among them: the warning through the punishments of nations, and what befell them, and that stories in which punishments are inflicted on criminals should be mentioned in the context of admonition and deterrence; just as it is fitting to mention what Allah has honored the people of piety with when encouraging and urging piety.

Among them: that Allah repels from the believers by many means, some of which they know and some of which they do not know at all; and sometimes He repels from them by means of their tribe and the disbelieving people of their homeland; as Allah repelled from Shu'ayb the stoning of his people by means of his clan.
And that these ties through which defense of Islam and Muslims is achieved are not objectionable to strive in; rather, it may even be required, because reform is sought according to ability and capacity. Accordingly, if Muslims living under the rule of disbelievers were to assist and work to make the rule a republic in which individuals and peoples can secure their religious and worldly rights, it would be better than their submission to a state that abolishes their religious and worldly rights, and seeks their annihilation and their reduction to laborers and servants. Yes; if it is possible for the state to belong to Muslims, with them as rulers, that is what is required; but since this rank is not attainable, the rank in which there is defense and protection for religion and worldly life takes precedence. And Allah knows best.

Among them: that the servant should be content with what Allah has given him, and be content with the lawful over the unlawful, and with permissible gains over forbidden gains; and that this is better for him, as in His saying: {What remains with Allah is better for you}; for in that there is blessing and increase of provision that is not found in eagerly pursuing forbidden means, which brings erasure and the opposite of blessing.
Among them: that this is among the requirements and fruits of faith; for He tied acting upon it to the existence of faith, which indicates that if the deed is not present, then faith is deficient or nonexistent.
Among them: that prayer has always been prescribed for the earlier prophets, and that it is among the best of deeds, to the extent that its excellence and its precedence over all other deeds are firmly established even among disbelievers; and that it forbids indecency and wrongdoing; and it is a measure of faith and its laws; so by establishing it the servant's condition is perfected, and by not establishing it his religious condition falls into disorder.
Among them: that the wealth which Allah provides for a person, even if Allah has granted it to him, is not for him to do with as he pleases; for it is a trust with him, and he must uphold Allah's right in it by fulfilling the rights that are due in it and refraining from the gains which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, not as the disbelievers and those like them claim, that their wealth is theirs to do with as they wish and choose, whether it agrees with the ruling of Allah or opposes it.
Among them: that it is part of completing and perfecting the call of the caller that he be the first to hasten to what he commands others to do, and the first to refrain from what he forbids others; as Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said: {And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you}, and as Allah, the Exalted, said: {O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? [It is most hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do]}.
Among them: that the duty, custom, and method of the messengers is to intend reform according to ability and capacity, so they bring about the attainment and perfecting of benefits, or the attainment of what is within their power of them, and the averting and reducing of harms; and they give precedence to public benefit over private benefit.
The reality of benefit (maslahah) is that by which the conditions of the servants are set right and their religious and worldly affairs are made upright.
Among them: that whoever undertakes what he is able of reform is not blameworthy or censured for not doing what he is unable to do; so the servant should establish, in himself and in others, the reform that he is able to.
Among them: that the servant should never rely on himself even for the blink of an eye, but should always seek help from his Lord, depending upon Him, asking Him for success; and if he attains any success, he should attribute it to the One who granted and bestowed it, and not be conceited with himself; as in His saying: {And my success is not but through Allah; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back}.
Among them: the warning through the punishments of nations, and what befell them, and that stories in which punishments are inflicted on criminals should be mentioned in the context of admonition and deterrence; just as it is fitting to mention what Allah has honored the people of piety with when encouraging and urging piety.
Among them: that the repentant from sin, just as he is pardoned and forgiven for his sin, Allah, the Exalted, loves him and is fond of him; and there is no weight to the saying of one who says that when the repentant repents, it is enough for him to be forgiven and for pardon to return to him, while the return of affection and love does not occur; for Allah said: {And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him; indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving}.
Among them: that Allah repels from the believers by many means, some of which they know and some of which they do not know at all; and sometimes He repels from them by means of their tribe and the disbelieving people of their homeland; as Allah repelled from Shu'ayb the stoning of his people by means of his clan.
And that these ties through which defense of Islam and Muslims is achieved are not objectionable to strive in; rather, it may even be required, because reform is sought according to ability and capacity. Accordingly, if Muslims living under the rule of disbelievers were to assist and work to make the rule a republic in which individuals and peoples can secure their religious and worldly rights, it would be better than their submission to a state that abolishes their religious and worldly rights, and seeks their annihilation and their reduction to laborers and servants. Yes; if it is possible for the state to belong to Muslims, with them as rulers, that is what is required; but since this rank is not attainable, the rank in which there is defense and protection for religion and worldly life takes precedence. And Allah knows best.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 11, verses 96–101:**

{96} He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We certainly sent Musa (Moses)﴾, the son of Imran, ﴿with Our signs﴾, which indicate the truth of what he brought, such as the staff and the hand and similar signs that God caused to appear at the hands of Musa, peace be upon him, ﴿and a clear authority﴾; that is, a manifest and evident proof that appeared as plainly as the sun.

{97} ﴿To Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his chiefs﴾; that is, the nobles of his people, because they were the ones who were followed, and others followed them. So they did not submit to what Musa brought of signs that he showed them, as has already been explained at length in Surah al-A'raf. Rather, ﴿they followed the command of Fir'awn, and the command of Fir'awn was not right-guiding﴾. Rather, he was misguided and astray, and commanded only what was pure harm.

{98} ﴿Without doubt﴾, when his people followed him, he led them to ruin and destroyed them. ﴿He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them to the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought.﴾

{99} ﴿And they were followed in this﴾, that is, in this world, ﴿by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection﴾; that is, God, His angels and all of mankind will curse them in this world and in the Hereafter. ﴿Wretched is the gift that is given﴾; that is, wretched is what has gathered for them and been added upon them of the punishment of God and the curse of this world and the Hereafter.

{100} When He mentioned the stories of these nations with their messengers, God said to His Messenger: ﴿That is from the reports of the cities which We relate to you﴾, so that you may warn by it, and so that it may be a sign of your prophethood, an admonition and a reminder for the believers. ﴿Of them some still stand﴾; that is, they were not destroyed completely, but some traces of their dwellings remain that indicate them. ﴿And some are mown down﴾; their dwellings have been demolished and their homes have been wiped out, so no trace of them remains.

{101} ﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ by seizing them with various kinds of punishment, ﴿but they wronged themselves﴾ through polytheism, disbelief and obstinacy. ﴿Their gods, whom they invoked besides God, did not avail them anything when the command of your Lord came﴾. Thus it is with everyone who turns to other than God: that does not benefit him when severe trials descend. ﴿And they added nothing to them but ruin﴾; that is, loss and destruction, contrary to what they had imagined.

{105} {On the Day it comes}: that Day, when creation is gathered, {no soul will speak except by His permission}: even the prophets and the noble angels will not intercede except by His permission. {Among them}; that is, among creation, {are wretched and happy}: the wretched are those who disbelieved in Allah, denied His messengers, and disobeyed His command, and the happy are the believers who are mindful of Allah.

{106} As for their recompense: {As for those who were wretched}; that is: wretchedness, disgrace, and humiliation befell them, {they will be in the Fire}: immersed in its punishment, its penalty severe upon them. {For them therein}: from the intensity of what they are in, {will be groaning and wailing}: and these are the most hideous and foul of sounds.

{107} {Abiding therein}; that is: in the Fire whose punishment is this, {for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills}; that is: they will abide therein forever, except for the period that Allah willed they would not be in it, and that is before entering it; as stated by the majority of the exegetes. So the exception, according to this, refers to the time before entering it; thus they abide therein for all times except the time before entering it. {Indeed, your Lord is an effecter of what He intends}: so whatever He wills and His wisdom requires, He does it, blessed and exalted is He, and no one can turn Him back from His will.

{109} Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So be not in doubt concerning what these worship﴾, namely the polytheists; i.e., do not doubt about their condition, and that what they are upon is falsehood. There is no legislative (shar'i) proof for them, nor any rational proof. Their only proof and basis of doubt is that they worship as their forefathers worshipped before them. It is well known that this is not even a doubt, let alone a proof, because the sayings of anyone other than the Prophets are to be examined and not taken as evidence, especially the sayings of such misguided people, whose errors are many and whose corruption of the foundations of religion is great. Their sayings, even if they agree upon them, are error and misguidance. ﴿And indeed, We will give them their portion undiminished﴾; i.e., their portion of this world, as has been decreed for them, must certainly reach them, even if that portion is abundant or pleasing to your eye. It does not indicate the soundness of their condition, for Allah gives worldly provision to whom He loves and whom He does not love, while He gives faith and the sound religion only to those whom He loves. The conclusion is that one should not be deceived by the agreement of the misguided upon the saying of their misguided forefathers of old, nor by what Allah has bestowed upon them and granted them of worldly goods.

{110} He, the Exalted, informs that He gave Musa the Book, which is the Torah, the thing that necessitates agreement upon its commands and prohibitions and unity. Yet despite this, those who ascribed themselves to it differed about it, in a way that harmed their beliefs and their religious unity. ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾: by His deferring them and not hastening their punishment. ﴿The matter would have been decided between them﴾: by bringing punishment upon the wrongdoer. But the Exalted, in His wisdom, decreed that He would delay the judgment between them until the Day of Resurrection, and they remained in disquieting doubt. If this was their condition with their own Book, then it is not strange that the group of Jews should not believe in the Qur'an that Allah revealed to you, and that they should be in disquieting doubt about it.

{111} ﴿And indeed, to each your Lord will surely pay in full for their deeds﴾: that is, Allah will certainly judge between them on the Day of Resurrection with His just judgment, recompensing each according to what he deserves. ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do﴾: of good and evil. ﴿Acquainted﴾: nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, whether minute or great.

{112} Then, when He informed of their lack of uprightness, which necessitated their disagreement and division, He commanded His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and those believers with him to be upright as they were commanded, to follow what Allah has legislated of laws, and to hold to the correct beliefs that Allah has informed of, and not to deviate from that to the right or to the left, and to persevere in that, and not to transgress by going beyond what Allah has set for them of uprightness. His saying ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾: that is, nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for them. In this is encouragement to follow uprightness and warning against its opposite.

{113} For this reason He warned them against inclining toward those who transgress uprightness, saying: ﴿And do not incline [i.e., do not lean]﴾ ﴿toward those who have wronged﴾: for if you incline toward them, you agree with them in their wrongdoing or are pleased with the wrong they are upon, ﴿lest the Fire touch you﴾ if you do that. ﴿And you would not have any protectors other than Allah﴾: who could prevent you from the punishment of Allah or obtain for you any reward from Allah. ﴿Then you would not be helped﴾: that is, the punishment would not be averted from you once it touched you.

In this verse is a warning against inclining toward any wrongdoer. The meaning of inclining (rukun) is leaning toward and aligning with the wrongdoer, agreeing with him in his wrongdoing, and being pleased with the wrong he is upon. If this threat is for inclining toward wrongdoers, then what of the wrongdoers themselves? We ask Allah for well-being from wrongdoing.
