Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 11, verses 114–115:

{114} Allah commands the establishment of the prayer in its entirety at "the two ends of the day" (ṭarafay al-nahār), that is, its beginning and its end. This includes the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-fajr) and the noon (ẓuhr) and afternoon ('aṣr) prayers. "And at the approaches of the night" (zulafan min al-layl): this includes the sunset (maghrib) and night ('ishā') prayers, and it also encompasses the night prayer (qiyām al-layl), for it is among the things that bring the servant near (tuzlifu) and draw him close (tuqarribuhu) to Allah, the Exalted. "Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds" (inna al-ḥasanāt yudhhibna al-sayyi'āt): that is, these five prayers and what is joined to them of voluntary acts (taṭawwu'āt) are among the greatest good deeds. Although they are good deeds that bring one near to Allah and entitle one to reward, they also remove and erase misdeeds (sayyi'āt). What is meant by this is minor sins (ṣaghā'ir), as specified by the authentic hadiths from the Prophet (ﷺ), such as his saying: "The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what lies between them, so long as major sins (kabā'ir) are avoided." Indeed, the verse in Surah al-Nisa' restricts it as well, where He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to an honourable entrance" (Q. 4:31). "That" (dhālika): perhaps the reference is to everything mentioned earlier: the necessity of steadfastness upon the straight path, not exceeding or transgressing it, not inclining toward those who do wrong, the command to establish the prayer, and the explanation that good deeds remove evil deeds. All of this is "a reminder for those who remember" (dhikrā li-l-dhākirīn): they understand through it what Allah has commanded and forbidden them, and they comply with those good commands which yield goodness and repel evils and misdeeds.

{115} But these matters require striving against the self (mujāhadat al-nafs) and patience upon them. For this reason He says: "And be patient" (wa-ṣbir): that is, restrain yourself upon obedience to Allah and away from disobedience to Him, bind yourself to that, persevere, and do not grow weary. "Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers" (fa-inna Allāh lā yuḍī'u ajra al-muḥsinīn): rather, Allah accepts from them the best of what they did and recompenses them with their reward according to the best of what they used to do.

In this there is a great encouragement to persist in patience, by stirring the weak soul with desire for Allah's reward whenever it becomes slack and lax.

{116} When Almighty God mentioned the destruction of the nations that denied the messengers, and that most of them had deviated from the people of the divine scriptures, and all of this leads religions towards extinction and decay, He mentioned that, had He not placed in the past generations remnants of the people of goodness, who call to guidance and forbid corruption and ruin, then benefit would not have come from them, and the religions would not have been preserved through them. But they are very few. The ultimate matter is that they were saved by following the messengers, by their upholding of the religion they were charged with, and by the establishing of God's proof through their hands, so that whoever perished would perish after clear evidence, and whoever lived would live after clear evidence. ﴿But those who did wrong followed the luxury they had been given﴾; that is, they followed what they were in of comfort and luxury, and did not seek any alternative to it. ﴿And they were criminals﴾; that is, they were wrongdoers by following what they had been given of luxury. Therefore the punishment became due upon them, and the torment uprooted them.

In this there is an exhortation to this Ummah that there should be remnants among them: reformers for what people have corrupted, standing up for the religion of God, calling those who have gone astray to guidance, patiently enduring harm from them, and giving them sight from blindness. This condition is the highest that those who seek to excel desire, and its possessor will be an imam in the religion if he makes his work sincere for the Lord of the worlds.

{117} That is: God would never destroy the towns through an injustice of His own towards them, while they were {muslihun}—that is, persisting in righteousness and continuing upon it. God would not destroy them except when they committed wrongdoing and the proof of God had been established against them.

It is also possible that the meaning is: your Lord would not destroy the towns for their earlier wrongdoing if they turn back and set their deeds right, for God pardons them and erases what preceded of their wrongdoing.

{118} He, exalted is He, informs that if He willed, He would have made mankind one community upon the Islamic religion, for His will is not deficient and nothing is beyond His capacity. But His wisdom required that they continue to differ, opposing the straight path, following the ways that lead to the Fire, each one seeing the truth in what he himself says and error in the words of others.

{119} {Except those upon whom your Lord has mercy}: He guides them to knowledge of the truth, to acting upon it, and to agreeing about it. These are the ones for whom the preceding happiness has been decreed, and upon whom divine care and Divine success have overtaken them. As for those other than them, they are forsaken and left to themselves. And His saying: {And for that He created them}; that is, His wisdom required that He created them so that among them there would be the happy and the wretched, the agreeing and the differing, the group whom Allah has guided and the group upon whom error has been justly decreed; so that His justice and wisdom would be made clear to the servants, and so that what lies hidden in human natures of good and evil would be made manifest, and so that the market of jihad and the acts of worship would be established, which are not completed or made upright except through trial and tribulation. {And} because {the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together"}: thus He must make ready for the Fire people who will work by its deeds that lead to it.

{120} When He mentioned in this surah some of the accounts of the prophets, He then stated the wisdom behind mentioning them, saying: ﴿And We relate to you from the news of the messengers that with which We strengthen your heart﴾. That is, [it strengthens] your heart, so that it may be at ease, steadfast, and patient, just as the people of resolve (ahl al-'azm) among the messengers were patient. Souls take comfort in following an example, are energized to act, and desire to compete with others. The truth is confirmed by mentioning its evidences and by the number of those who upheld it. ﴿And there has come to you in this﴾ surah ﴿the truth﴾, that is, certainty, so there is no doubt in it in any respect. Knowledge of this is part of knowledge of the truth, which is the greatest virtue of souls. ﴿And an admonition and a reminder for the believers﴾, that is, they take admonition from it and refrain from disliked matters, and they remember the matters that are beloved to God and do them.

{121} As for those who are not of the people of faith, admonitions and various kinds of reminder do not benefit them. For this reason He said: ﴿And say to those who do not believe﴾, after the signs have been established against them: ﴿Act according to your standing﴾, that is, your state in which you are, ﴿indeed, we are acting﴾ according to what we have been upon.

{122} ﴿And wait﴾ for what will befall us, ﴿indeed, we are waiting﴾ for what will befall you.

{123} God has distinguished between the two groups, and has shown His servants His victory for His believing servants and His subjugation of the enemies of God who denied. ﴿And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, what is hidden in them of concealed things and unseen matters. ﴿And to Him the whole matter will be returned﴾, [namely] the deeds and the doers, so He will distinguish the wicked from the good. ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾, that is, devote yourself to His worship, which is all that God has commanded of what you are able to do. ﴿And rely upon God﴾ in that. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾, of good and evil; rather, His knowledge encompasses that, His pen has recorded it, and His judgment and recompense will apply to it.

The commentary (tafsir) of Surah Hud is complete.
And all praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds. May God send blessings and peace upon Muhammad (ﷺ). The completion of its copying was on Saturday, the 21st of Rabi' al-Akhir, in the year 1347.
